    <ix:nonNumeric name="us-gaap:OrganizationConsolidationAndPresentationOfFinancialStatementsDisclosureAndSignificantAccountingPoliciesTextBlock" id="Text_136daea87f7d4006bb5e277cd264168f" contextRef="c20250101to20251231" escape="true" continuedAt="Text_c4d5dd92edac4e12aff80ee0dd02daa61">
<div style="text-align: justify; font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;"><span style="font-size: 10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-weight: bold;">1.</span>&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;<span style="font-size: 10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-weight: bold;">Summary of Significant Accounting Policies</span></div>
</ix:nonNumeric>
    <div style="text-align: justify; font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">
      <ix:continuation id="Text_c4d5dd92edac4e12aff80ee0dd02daa61" continuedAt="Text_c4d5dd92edac4e12aff80ee0dd02daa62"><hr style="height: 2px; color: #000000; background-color: #000000; text-align: center; border: none; margin-left: auto; margin-right: auto;"/></ix:continuation></div>

    <ix:continuation id="Text_c4d5dd92edac4e12aff80ee0dd02daa62" continuedAt="Text_c4d5dd92edac4e12aff80ee0dd02daa63">
<div><br/>
    </div>
</ix:continuation>
    <ix:continuation id="Text_c4d5dd92edac4e12aff80ee0dd02daa63" continuedAt="Text_c4d5dd92edac4e12aff80ee0dd02daa64">
<div style="text-align: justify; font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">The accounting and reporting policies of NBT Bancorp Inc. and its subsidiaries, NBT Bank, National Association (&#8220;NBT Bank&#8221; or the &#8220;Bank&#8221;), NBT Financial Services, Inc.
      and NBT Holdings, Inc., conform, in all material respects, with U.S. generally accepted accounting principles (&#8220;GAAP&#8221;) and to general practices within the banking industry. Collectively, NBT Bancorp Inc. and its subsidiaries are referred to herein as
      (the &#8220;Company&#8221;).</div>
</ix:continuation>
    <ix:continuation id="Text_c4d5dd92edac4e12aff80ee0dd02daa64" continuedAt="Text_c4d5dd92edac4e12aff80ee0dd02daa65">
<div><br/>
    </div>
</ix:continuation>

    <ix:continuation id="Text_c4d5dd92edac4e12aff80ee0dd02daa65" continuedAt="Text_c4d5dd92edac4e12aff80ee0dd02daa66"><ix:nonNumeric name="us-gaap:BasisOfAccountingPolicyPolicyTextBlock" id="Text_658e2b3f016c4b8fbc9d39aa99b8ee15" contextRef="c20250101to20251231" escape="true">
<div style="text-align: justify; font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">The preparation of financial statements in conformity with GAAP requires management to make estimates and assumptions that affect the reported amounts in the financial
      statements and accompanying notes. Actual results may differ from those estimates and such differences could be material to the financial statements. </div>
</ix:nonNumeric></ix:continuation>
    <ix:continuation id="Text_c4d5dd92edac4e12aff80ee0dd02daa66" continuedAt="Text_c4d5dd92edac4e12aff80ee0dd02daa67">
<div style="text-align: justify; font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;"> <br/>
    </div>
</ix:continuation>

    <ix:nonNumeric name="us-gaap:UseOfEstimates" id="Text_f824f7cc1fa14a61ba0568ede18acd77" contextRef="c20250101to20251231" escape="true"><ix:continuation id="Text_c4d5dd92edac4e12aff80ee0dd02daa67" continuedAt="Text_c4d5dd92edac4e12aff80ee0dd02daa68">
<div style="text-align: justify; font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">Estimates associated with the allowance for credit losses are particularly susceptible to material change in the near term.</div>
</ix:continuation></ix:nonNumeric>

    <ix:continuation id="Text_c4d5dd92edac4e12aff80ee0dd02daa68" continuedAt="Text_c4d5dd92edac4e12aff80ee0dd02daa69">
<div><br/>
    </div>
</ix:continuation>
    <ix:continuation id="Text_c4d5dd92edac4e12aff80ee0dd02daa69" continuedAt="Text_c4d5dd92edac4e12aff80ee0dd02daa610">
<div style="text-align: justify; font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">The following is a description of significant policies and practices:</div>
</ix:continuation>
    <ix:continuation id="Text_c4d5dd92edac4e12aff80ee0dd02daa610" continuedAt="Text_c4d5dd92edac4e12aff80ee0dd02daa611">
<div><br/>
    </div>
</ix:continuation>

    <ix:nonNumeric name="us-gaap:ConsolidationPolicyTextBlock" id="Text_aff232905746429e891aaeb317179ca6" contextRef="c20250101to20251231" escape="true" continuedAt="Text_f7811deea5c14afdb0ae157bdd6a0b971"><ix:continuation id="Text_c4d5dd92edac4e12aff80ee0dd02daa611" continuedAt="Text_c4d5dd92edac4e12aff80ee0dd02daa612">
<div style="text-align: justify; font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; font-weight: bold;">Consolidation</div>
</ix:continuation></ix:nonNumeric>
    <ix:continuation id="Text_f7811deea5c14afdb0ae157bdd6a0b971" continuedAt="Text_f7811deea5c14afdb0ae157bdd6a0b972"><ix:continuation id="Text_c4d5dd92edac4e12aff80ee0dd02daa612" continuedAt="Text_c4d5dd92edac4e12aff80ee0dd02daa613">
<div><br/>
    </div>
</ix:continuation></ix:continuation>
    <div>
      <ix:continuation id="Text_f7811deea5c14afdb0ae157bdd6a0b972" continuedAt="Text_f7811deea5c14afdb0ae157bdd6a0b973"><ix:continuation id="Text_c4d5dd92edac4e12aff80ee0dd02daa613" continuedAt="Text_c4d5dd92edac4e12aff80ee0dd02daa614">
<div style="text-align: justify; color: rgb(0, 0, 0); font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">The accompanying consolidated financial statements include the accounts of NBT Bancorp Inc. and its wholly-owned subsidiaries mentioned above. All
        material intercompany transactions have been eliminated in consolidation. Amounts previously reported in the consolidated financial statements are reclassified whenever necessary to conform to the current year&#8217;s presentation. In the &#8220;Parent Company
        Financial Information,&#8221; the investment in subsidiaries is recorded using the equity method of accounting.</div>
</ix:continuation></ix:continuation>
    </div>

    <ix:continuation id="Text_f7811deea5c14afdb0ae157bdd6a0b973" continuedAt="Text_f7811deea5c14afdb0ae157bdd6a0b974"><ix:continuation id="Text_c4d5dd92edac4e12aff80ee0dd02daa614" continuedAt="Text_c4d5dd92edac4e12aff80ee0dd02daa615">
<div><br/>
    </div>
</ix:continuation></ix:continuation>
    <ix:continuation id="Text_f7811deea5c14afdb0ae157bdd6a0b974"><ix:continuation id="Text_c4d5dd92edac4e12aff80ee0dd02daa615" continuedAt="Text_c4d5dd92edac4e12aff80ee0dd02daa616">
<div style="text-align: justify; font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">The Company determines whether it has a controlling financial interest in an entity by first evaluating whether the entity is a voting interest entity or a variable
      interest entity under GAAP. Voting interest entities are entities in which the total equity investment at risk is sufficient to enable the entity to finance itself independently and provides the equity holders with the obligation to absorb losses,
      the right to receive residual returns and the right to make decisions about the entity&#8217;s activities. The Company consolidates voting interest entities in which it has all, or at least a majority of, the voting interest. As defined in applicable
      accounting standards, variable interest entities (&#8220;VIEs&#8221;) are entities that lack one or more of the characteristics of a voting interest entity. A controlling financial interest in a VIE is present when the Company has both the power and ability to
      direct the activities of the VIE that most significantly impact the VIE&#8217;s economic performance and an obligation to absorb losses or the right to receive benefits that could potentially be significant to the VIE. The Company&#8217;s wholly-owned
      subsidiaries CNBF Capital Trust I, NBT Statutory Trust I, NBT Statutory Trust II, Alliance Financial Capital Trust I, Alliance Financial Capital Trust II and Evans Capital Trust I are VIEs for which the Company is not the primary beneficiary.
      Accordingly, the accounts of these entities are not included in the Company&#8217;s consolidated financial statements.</div>
</ix:continuation></ix:continuation>

    <ix:continuation id="Text_c4d5dd92edac4e12aff80ee0dd02daa616" continuedAt="Text_c4d5dd92edac4e12aff80ee0dd02daa617">
<div><br/>
    </div>
</ix:continuation>

    <ix:nonNumeric name="us-gaap:SegmentReportingPolicyPolicyTextBlock" id="Text_7350a65e00c8494a9d4d888d3a241f24" contextRef="c20250101to20251231" escape="true" continuedAt="Text_844a6f8e60dd4ebebb3fd8a63d3bb12b1"><ix:continuation id="Text_c4d5dd92edac4e12aff80ee0dd02daa617" continuedAt="Text_c4d5dd92edac4e12aff80ee0dd02daa618">
<div style="text-align: justify; font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; font-weight: bold;">Segment Reporting</div>
</ix:continuation></ix:nonNumeric>
    <ix:continuation id="Text_844a6f8e60dd4ebebb3fd8a63d3bb12b1" continuedAt="Text_844a6f8e60dd4ebebb3fd8a63d3bb12b2"><ix:continuation id="Text_c4d5dd92edac4e12aff80ee0dd02daa618" continuedAt="Text_c4d5dd92edac4e12aff80ee0dd02daa619">
<div><br/>
    </div>
</ix:continuation></ix:continuation>
    <ix:continuation id="Text_844a6f8e60dd4ebebb3fd8a63d3bb12b2" continuedAt="Text_844a6f8e60dd4ebebb3fd8a63d3bb12b3"><ix:continuation id="Text_c4d5dd92edac4e12aff80ee0dd02daa619" continuedAt="Text_c4d5dd92edac4e12aff80ee0dd02daa620">
<div style="text-align: justify; font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; font-weight: normal; color: rgb(0, 0, 0); font-style: normal; font-variant: normal; text-transform: none;">The Company&#8217;s operations are primarily in the community banking
      industry and include the provision of traditional banking services.&#160;The Company also provides other services through its subsidiaries such as insurance, retirement plan administration and wealth management. The Company operates in the geographical
      regions of upstate New York, northeastern Pennsylvania, southern New Hampshire, western Massachusetts, Vermont, southern Maine and central and northwestern Connecticut. </div>
</ix:continuation></ix:continuation>
    <ix:continuation id="Text_844a6f8e60dd4ebebb3fd8a63d3bb12b3" continuedAt="Text_844a6f8e60dd4ebebb3fd8a63d3bb12b4"><ix:continuation id="Text_c4d5dd92edac4e12aff80ee0dd02daa620" continuedAt="Text_c4d5dd92edac4e12aff80ee0dd02daa621">
<div><span style="font-weight: normal; color: rgb(0, 0, 0); font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; font-style: normal; font-variant: normal; text-transform: none;"> </span></div>
</ix:continuation></ix:continuation>
    <div style="text-align: justify; font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;"><ix:continuation id="Text_844a6f8e60dd4ebebb3fd8a63d3bb12b4" continuedAt="Text_844a6f8e60dd4ebebb3fd8a63d3bb12b5"><ix:continuation id="Text_c4d5dd92edac4e12aff80ee0dd02daa621" continuedAt="Text_c4d5dd92edac4e12aff80ee0dd02daa622">
<div><span style="font-size: 10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman'; color: rgb(0, 0, 0); font-weight: normal; font-style: normal; font-variant: normal; text-transform: none;">
        <br/>
      </span></div>
</ix:continuation></ix:continuation>
      <ix:continuation id="Text_844a6f8e60dd4ebebb3fd8a63d3bb12b5" continuedAt="Text_844a6f8e60dd4ebebb3fd8a63d3bb12b6"><ix:continuation id="Text_c4d5dd92edac4e12aff80ee0dd02daa622" continuedAt="Text_c4d5dd92edac4e12aff80ee0dd02daa623">
<div style="text-align: justify; font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; font-weight: normal; color: rgb(0, 0, 0); font-style: normal; font-variant: normal; text-transform: none;">The Company manages its operations under the segments of
        Banking, including Wealth Management, Retirement Plan Administration and Insurance. Prior to the fourth quarter of 2024, the Company disclosed a <span style="-sec-ix-hidden:Fact_907f0c7c3a974a8a90512937c7fb0b22">single</span>
        reportable segment, as revenue from individual segments were below the disclosure threshold relative to consolidated revenue, total assets and operating profit or loss. Each year the Company evaluates its business activities, financial results and
        operational data to determine whether segment disclosure is required.</div>
</ix:continuation></ix:continuation>
      <ix:continuation id="Text_844a6f8e60dd4ebebb3fd8a63d3bb12b6" continuedAt="Text_844a6f8e60dd4ebebb3fd8a63d3bb12b7"><ix:continuation id="Text_c4d5dd92edac4e12aff80ee0dd02daa623" continuedAt="Text_c4d5dd92edac4e12aff80ee0dd02daa624">
<div style="text-align: left; color: #000000; font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;"> <span style="font-weight: normal; color: rgb(0, 0, 0); font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; font-style: normal; font-variant: normal; text-transform: none;"><br/>
        </span></div>
</ix:continuation></ix:continuation>
      <div style="text-align: left; color: #000000; font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">
        <ix:continuation id="Text_844a6f8e60dd4ebebb3fd8a63d3bb12b7"><ix:continuation id="Text_c4d5dd92edac4e12aff80ee0dd02daa624" continuedAt="Text_c4d5dd92edac4e12aff80ee0dd02daa625">
<div style="text-align: justify; font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; font-weight: normal; color: rgb(0, 0, 0); font-style: normal; font-variant: normal; text-transform: none;">In accordance with Accounting Standards Update (&#8220;ASU&#8221;)
          2023-07, <span style="font-style: italic;">Segment Reporting (Topic 280): Improvements to Reportable Segment Disclosures</span>, management assesses its operating segment structure to enhance transparency in how financial performance is
          evaluated and resources are allocated by the chief operating decision maker (&#8220;CODM&#8221;). The Company has determined that it operates through <ix:nonFraction name="us-gaap:NumberOfReportableSegments" id="Fact_b9e274d43f2f49998bc11467092cf285" contextRef="c20250101to20251231" unitRef="U004" decimals="INF" scale="0" format="ixt-sec:numwordsen">two</ix:nonFraction>
          reportable segments: Banking and Retirement Plan Administration, as they meet both the quantitative threshold and qualitative criteria for disclosure. Wealth Management is combined with our Banking segment in accordance with the similarity test
          outlined in ASC 280. Insurance does not meet materiality requirements for disclosure and is included in the &#8220;All Other&#8221; category.</div>
</ix:continuation></ix:continuation>
      </div>

    </div>
<ix:continuation id="Text_c4d5dd92edac4e12aff80ee0dd02daa625" continuedAt="Text_c4d5dd92edac4e12aff80ee0dd02daa626">

    <span style="font-weight: normal; color: rgb(0, 0, 0); font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; font-style: normal; font-variant: normal; text-transform: none;"> </span></div>
</ix:continuation>

    <ix:nonNumeric name="us-gaap:CashAndCashEquivalentsPolicyTextBlock" id="Text_850f4652b1ad44d399360a62d41a2db1" contextRef="c20250101to20251231" escape="true" continuedAt="Text_756ca4b9a32947d2b5724dca73b3a6141"><ix:continuation id="Text_c4d5dd92edac4e12aff80ee0dd02daa627" continuedAt="Text_c4d5dd92edac4e12aff80ee0dd02daa628">
<div style="text-align: justify; font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; font-weight: bold;">Cash Equivalents</div>
</ix:continuation></ix:nonNumeric>
    <ix:continuation id="Text_756ca4b9a32947d2b5724dca73b3a6141" continuedAt="Text_756ca4b9a32947d2b5724dca73b3a6142"><ix:continuation id="Text_c4d5dd92edac4e12aff80ee0dd02daa628" continuedAt="Text_c4d5dd92edac4e12aff80ee0dd02daa629">

    <ix:continuation id="Text_756ca4b9a32947d2b5724dca73b3a6142"><ix:continuation id="Text_c4d5dd92edac4e12aff80ee0dd02daa629" continuedAt="Text_c4d5dd92edac4e12aff80ee0dd02daa630">

    <ix:nonNumeric name="us-gaap:MarketableSecuritiesPolicy" id="Text_0ef60a126ad242b7b49e46d016911c90" contextRef="c20250101to20251231" escape="true" continuedAt="Text_10f0a06d63d84c6db793aafaffd9aaf01"><ix:continuation id="Text_c4d5dd92edac4e12aff80ee0dd02daa631" continuedAt="Text_c4d5dd92edac4e12aff80ee0dd02daa632">
<div style="text-align: justify; font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; font-weight: bold;">Securities</div>
</ix:continuation></ix:nonNumeric>
    <ix:continuation id="Text_10f0a06d63d84c6db793aafaffd9aaf01" continuedAt="Text_10f0a06d63d84c6db793aafaffd9aaf02"><ix:continuation id="Text_c4d5dd92edac4e12aff80ee0dd02daa632" continuedAt="Text_c4d5dd92edac4e12aff80ee0dd02daa633">
<div><br/>
    </div>
</ix:continuation></ix:continuation>
    <ix:continuation id="Text_10f0a06d63d84c6db793aafaffd9aaf02" continuedAt="Text_10f0a06d63d84c6db793aafaffd9aaf03"><ix:continuation id="Text_c4d5dd92edac4e12aff80ee0dd02daa633" continuedAt="Text_c4d5dd92edac4e12aff80ee0dd02daa634">
<div style="text-align: justify; font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">The Company classifies its securities at date of purchase as either held to maturity (&#8220;HTM&#8221;), available for sale (&#8220;AFS&#8221;) or equity. HTM debt securities are those that
      the Company has the ability and intent to hold until maturity. AFS debt securities are securities that are not classified as HTM. AFS securities are recorded at fair value. Unrealized holding gains and losses, net of the related tax effect, on AFS
      securities are excluded from earnings and are reported in the consolidated statements of changes in stockholders&#8217; equity and the consolidated statements of comprehensive income (loss) as a component of accumulated other comprehensive income (loss)
      (&#8220;AOCI&#8221;). HTM securities are recorded at amortized cost. Transfers of securities between categories are recorded at fair value at the date of transfer. Non-marketable equity securities and equity securities without readily determinable fair values
      are carried at cost. The Company performs a qualitative assessment on equity securities to determine whether the investments are impaired and downward or upward adjustments are recognized through the income statement. All other equity securities are
      recorded at fair value, with net unrealized gains and losses recognized in income.</div>
</ix:continuation></ix:continuation>
    <ix:continuation id="Text_10f0a06d63d84c6db793aafaffd9aaf03" continuedAt="Text_10f0a06d63d84c6db793aafaffd9aaf04"><ix:continuation id="Text_c4d5dd92edac4e12aff80ee0dd02daa634" continuedAt="Text_c4d5dd92edac4e12aff80ee0dd02daa635">
<div><br/>
    </div>
</ix:continuation></ix:continuation>
    <ix:continuation id="Text_10f0a06d63d84c6db793aafaffd9aaf04" continuedAt="Text_10f0a06d63d84c6db793aafaffd9aaf05"><ix:continuation id="Text_c4d5dd92edac4e12aff80ee0dd02daa635" continuedAt="Text_c4d5dd92edac4e12aff80ee0dd02daa636">
<div style="text-align: justify; font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">Premiums and discounts are amortized or accreted over the life of the related security as an adjustment to yield using the interest method. Dividend and interest income
      are recognized when earned. Realized gains and losses on securities sold are derived using the specific identification method for determining the cost of securities sold.</div>
</ix:continuation></ix:continuation>
    <ix:continuation id="Text_10f0a06d63d84c6db793aafaffd9aaf05" continuedAt="Text_10f0a06d63d84c6db793aafaffd9aaf06"><ix:continuation id="Text_c4d5dd92edac4e12aff80ee0dd02daa636" continuedAt="Text_c4d5dd92edac4e12aff80ee0dd02daa637">
<div style="text-align: justify; font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;"> <br/>
    </div>
</ix:continuation></ix:continuation>
    <ix:continuation id="Text_10f0a06d63d84c6db793aafaffd9aaf06" continuedAt="Text_10f0a06d63d84c6db793aafaffd9aaf07"><ix:continuation id="Text_c4d5dd92edac4e12aff80ee0dd02daa637" continuedAt="Text_c4d5dd92edac4e12aff80ee0dd02daa638">
<div style="text-align: justify; font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;"> Investments in Federal Reserve Board (&#8220;FRB&#8221;) and Federal Home Loan Bank (&#8220;FHLB&#8221;) stock are required for membership in those organizations and are carried at cost since
      there is no market value available. The FHLB New York continues to pay dividends and repurchase stock. As such, the Company has not recognized any impairment on its holdings of FRB and FHLB stock. </div>
</ix:continuation></ix:continuation>
    <ix:continuation id="Text_10f0a06d63d84c6db793aafaffd9aaf07" continuedAt="Text_10f0a06d63d84c6db793aafaffd9aaf08"><ix:continuation id="Text_c4d5dd92edac4e12aff80ee0dd02daa638" continuedAt="Text_c4d5dd92edac4e12aff80ee0dd02daa639">
<div><br/>
    </div>
</ix:continuation></ix:continuation>
    <ix:continuation id="Text_10f0a06d63d84c6db793aafaffd9aaf08" continuedAt="Text_10f0a06d63d84c6db793aafaffd9aaf09"><ix:continuation id="Text_c4d5dd92edac4e12aff80ee0dd02daa639" continuedAt="Text_c4d5dd92edac4e12aff80ee0dd02daa640">
<div style="text-align: justify; color: rgb(0, 0, 0); font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; font-style: italic;">Allowance for Credit Losses &#8211; HTM Debt Securities</div>
</ix:continuation></ix:continuation>
    <ix:continuation id="Text_10f0a06d63d84c6db793aafaffd9aaf09" continuedAt="Text_10f0a06d63d84c6db793aafaffd9aaf010"><ix:continuation id="Text_c4d5dd92edac4e12aff80ee0dd02daa640" continuedAt="Text_c4d5dd92edac4e12aff80ee0dd02daa641">
<div><br/>
    </div>
</ix:continuation></ix:continuation>
    <ix:continuation id="Text_10f0a06d63d84c6db793aafaffd9aaf010" continuedAt="Text_10f0a06d63d84c6db793aafaffd9aaf011"><ix:continuation id="Text_c4d5dd92edac4e12aff80ee0dd02daa641" continuedAt="Text_c4d5dd92edac4e12aff80ee0dd02daa642">
<div style="text-align: justify; color: rgb(0, 0, 0); font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">With respect to its HTM debt securities, the Company is required to utilize the Financial Accounting Standards Board (&#8220;FASB&#8221;) ASU 2016-13, <span style="font-style: italic;">Financial Instruments - Credit Losses (Topic 326): Measurement of Credit Losses on Financial Instruments</span> methodology to estimate expected credit losses. Management measures expected credit losses on HTM debt
      securities on a collective basis by major security types that share similar risk characteristics, such as (as applicable): internal or external (third-party) credit score or credit ratings, risk ratings or classification, financial asset type,
      collateral type, size, effective interest rate, term, geographical location, industry of the borrower, vintage, historical or expected credit loss patterns, and reasonable and supportable forecast periods. Management classifies the HTM portfolio into
      the following major security types: U.S. government agency or U.S. government-sponsored mortgage-backed and collateralized mortgage obligations securities, and state and municipal debt securities.</div>
</ix:continuation></ix:continuation>
    <ix:continuation id="Text_10f0a06d63d84c6db793aafaffd9aaf011" continuedAt="Text_10f0a06d63d84c6db793aafaffd9aaf012"><ix:continuation id="Text_c4d5dd92edac4e12aff80ee0dd02daa642" continuedAt="Text_c4d5dd92edac4e12aff80ee0dd02daa643">
<div><br/>
    </div>
</ix:continuation></ix:continuation>
    <ix:continuation id="Text_10f0a06d63d84c6db793aafaffd9aaf012" continuedAt="Text_10f0a06d63d84c6db793aafaffd9aaf013"><ix:continuation id="Text_c4d5dd92edac4e12aff80ee0dd02daa643" continuedAt="Text_c4d5dd92edac4e12aff80ee0dd02daa644">
<div style="text-align: justify; color: rgb(0, 0, 0); font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">The HTM mortgage-backed and collateralized mortgage obligations securities are issued by U.S. government agencies or U.S. government-sponsored
      enterprises. These securities are either explicitly and/or implicitly guaranteed by the U.S. government as to timely repayment of principal and interest, are highly rated by major rating agencies, and have a long history of zero credit losses.
      Therefore, the Company did not record an allowance for credit loss for these securities.</div>
</ix:continuation></ix:continuation>
    <ix:continuation id="Text_10f0a06d63d84c6db793aafaffd9aaf013" continuedAt="Text_10f0a06d63d84c6db793aafaffd9aaf014"><ix:continuation id="Text_c4d5dd92edac4e12aff80ee0dd02daa644" continuedAt="Text_c4d5dd92edac4e12aff80ee0dd02daa645">
<div><br/>
    </div>
</ix:continuation></ix:continuation>
    <ix:continuation id="Text_10f0a06d63d84c6db793aafaffd9aaf014" continuedAt="Text_10f0a06d63d84c6db793aafaffd9aaf015"><ix:continuation id="Text_c4d5dd92edac4e12aff80ee0dd02daa645" continuedAt="Text_c4d5dd92edac4e12aff80ee0dd02daa646">
<div style="text-align: justify; color: rgb(0, 0, 0); font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">State and municipal bonds generally carry a Moody&#8217;s rating of A to AAA. In addition, the Company has a limited amount of New York state local
      municipal bonds that are not rated. The estimate of expected credit losses on the HTM portfolio is based on the expected cash flows of each individual bond over its contractual life and considers historical credit loss information, current conditions
      and reasonable and supportable forecasts. Given the rarity of municipal defaults and losses, the Company utilized Moody&#8217;s Municipal Loss Forecast Model as the sole source of municipal default and loss rates which provides decades of data across all
      municipal sectors and geographies. As with the loan portfolio, cash flows are forecast over a 6-quarter period under various weighted economic conditions, with a reversion to long-term average economic conditions over a 4-quarter period on a
      straight-line basis. Management may exercise discretion to make adjustments based on environmental factors. The Company determined that the expected credit loss on its HTM municipal bond portfolio was deemed immaterial, therefore <ix:nonFraction name="us-gaap:DebtSecuritiesHeldToMaturityCreditLossExpenseReversal" id="Fact_b227026f5b8948d9b4103e1f400ec1c3" contextRef="c20250101to20251231" unitRef="U001" decimals="-3" scale="3" format="ixt-sec:numwordsen">no</ix:nonFraction> allowance for credit losses was recorded.</div>
</ix:continuation></ix:continuation>
    <ix:continuation id="Text_10f0a06d63d84c6db793aafaffd9aaf015" continuedAt="Text_10f0a06d63d84c6db793aafaffd9aaf016"><ix:continuation id="Text_c4d5dd92edac4e12aff80ee0dd02daa646" continuedAt="Text_c4d5dd92edac4e12aff80ee0dd02daa647">
<div><br/>
    </div>
</ix:continuation></ix:continuation>
    <ix:continuation id="Text_10f0a06d63d84c6db793aafaffd9aaf016" continuedAt="Text_10f0a06d63d84c6db793aafaffd9aaf017"><ix:continuation id="Text_c4d5dd92edac4e12aff80ee0dd02daa647" continuedAt="Text_c4d5dd92edac4e12aff80ee0dd02daa648">
<div style="text-align: justify; color: rgb(0, 0, 0); font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; font-style: italic;">Allowance for Credit Losses &#8211; AFS Debt Securities</div>
</ix:continuation></ix:continuation>
    <ix:continuation id="Text_10f0a06d63d84c6db793aafaffd9aaf017" continuedAt="Text_10f0a06d63d84c6db793aafaffd9aaf018"><ix:continuation id="Text_c4d5dd92edac4e12aff80ee0dd02daa648" continuedAt="Text_c4d5dd92edac4e12aff80ee0dd02daa649">
<div><br/>
    </div>
</ix:continuation></ix:continuation>
    <ix:continuation id="Text_10f0a06d63d84c6db793aafaffd9aaf018"><ix:continuation id="Text_c4d5dd92edac4e12aff80ee0dd02daa649" continuedAt="Text_c4d5dd92edac4e12aff80ee0dd02daa650">
<div style="text-align: justify; color: rgb(0, 0, 0); font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">The impairment model for AFS debt securities differs from the current expected credit losses (&#8220;CECL&#8221;) methodology utilized for HTM debt securities
      because AFS debt securities are measured at fair value rather than amortized cost. For AFS debt securities in an unrealized loss position, the Company first assesses whether it intends to sell, or it is more likely than not that it will be required
      to sell the security before recovery of their amortized cost basis. If either of the criteria regarding intent or requirement to sell is met, the security&#8217;s amortized cost basis is written down to fair value through income. For AFS debt securities
      that do not meet the aforementioned criteria, in making this assessment, management considers the extent to which fair value is less than amortized cost, any changes to the rating of the security by a rating agency, adverse conditions specifically
      related to the security, failure of the issuer of the debt security to make scheduled interest or principal payments, among other factors. If this assessment indicates that a credit loss exists, the present value of cash flows expected to be
      collected from the security are compared to the amortized cost basis of the security. The cash flows should be estimated using information relevant to the collectability of the security, including information about past events, current conditions and
      reasonable and supportable forecasts. If the present value of cash flows expected to be collected is less than the amortized cost basis, a credit loss exists and an allowance for credit losses is recorded for the credit loss, limited by the amount
      that the fair value is less than the amortized cost basis. Any impairment that has not been recorded through an allowance for credit losses is recognized in other comprehensive income.</div>
</ix:continuation></ix:continuation>

    <ix:continuation id="Text_c4d5dd92edac4e12aff80ee0dd02daa650" continuedAt="Text_c4d5dd92edac4e12aff80ee0dd02daa651">
<div><br/>
    </div>
</ix:continuation>

    <ix:nonNumeric name="nbtb:LoanHeldForSaleAndLoanServicingPolicyPolicyTextBlock" id="Text_cb79706e40ba4f6db05e5c6e3a1f7101" contextRef="c20250101to20251231" escape="true" continuedAt="Text_f643cf790d7641c1b8ff197658bcbdfb1"><ix:continuation id="Text_c4d5dd92edac4e12aff80ee0dd02daa651" continuedAt="Text_c4d5dd92edac4e12aff80ee0dd02daa652">
<div style="text-align: justify; font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; font-weight: bold;">Loan Held for Sale and Loan Servicing</div>
</ix:continuation></ix:nonNumeric>
    <ix:continuation id="Text_f643cf790d7641c1b8ff197658bcbdfb1" continuedAt="Text_f643cf790d7641c1b8ff197658bcbdfb2"><ix:continuation id="Text_c4d5dd92edac4e12aff80ee0dd02daa652" continuedAt="Text_c4d5dd92edac4e12aff80ee0dd02daa653">
<div><br/>
    </div>
</ix:continuation></ix:continuation>
    <ix:continuation id="Text_f643cf790d7641c1b8ff197658bcbdfb2"><ix:continuation id="Text_c4d5dd92edac4e12aff80ee0dd02daa653" continuedAt="Text_c4d5dd92edac4e12aff80ee0dd02daa654">
<div style="text-align: justify; font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">Loans held for sale are recorded at the lower of cost or fair value on an individual basis. Loan sales are recorded when the sales are funded. Gains and losses on sales
      of loans held for sale are included in other noninterest income in the consolidated statements of income. Mortgage loans held for sale are generally sold with servicing rights retained. Mortgage servicing rights are recorded at fair value upon sale
      of the loan, and are amortized in proportion to and over the period of estimated net servicing income.</div>
</ix:continuation></ix:continuation>

    <ix:continuation id="Text_c4d5dd92edac4e12aff80ee0dd02daa654" continuedAt="Text_c4d5dd92edac4e12aff80ee0dd02daa655">

    <ix:nonNumeric name="us-gaap:FinanceLoansAndLeasesReceivablePolicy" id="Text_8b82cbc652094972b2bca8aca1316734" contextRef="c20250101to20251231" escape="true" continuedAt="Text_497348934d334eaeb3b059bf54cbfbe31"><ix:continuation id="Text_c4d5dd92edac4e12aff80ee0dd02daa655" continuedAt="Text_c4d5dd92edac4e12aff80ee0dd02daa656">
<div style="text-align: justify; font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; font-weight: bold;">Loans</div>
</ix:continuation></ix:nonNumeric>
    <ix:continuation id="Text_497348934d334eaeb3b059bf54cbfbe31" continuedAt="Text_497348934d334eaeb3b059bf54cbfbe32"><ix:continuation id="Text_c4d5dd92edac4e12aff80ee0dd02daa656" continuedAt="Text_c4d5dd92edac4e12aff80ee0dd02daa657">
<div><br/>
    </div>
</ix:continuation></ix:continuation>
    <ix:continuation id="Text_497348934d334eaeb3b059bf54cbfbe32" continuedAt="Text_497348934d334eaeb3b059bf54cbfbe33"><ix:continuation id="Text_c4d5dd92edac4e12aff80ee0dd02daa657" continuedAt="Text_c4d5dd92edac4e12aff80ee0dd02daa658">
<div style="text-align: justify; font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">Loans are recorded at their current unpaid principal balance, net of unearned income and unamortized loan fees and expenses, which are amortized under the effective
      interest method over the estimated lives of the loans. Interest income on loans is accrued based on the principal amount outstanding.</div>
</ix:continuation></ix:continuation>
    <ix:continuation id="Text_497348934d334eaeb3b059bf54cbfbe33" continuedAt="Text_497348934d334eaeb3b059bf54cbfbe34"><ix:continuation id="Text_c4d5dd92edac4e12aff80ee0dd02daa658" continuedAt="Text_c4d5dd92edac4e12aff80ee0dd02daa659">
<div><br/>

</ix:continuation></ix:continuation>
    <ix:continuation id="Text_497348934d334eaeb3b059bf54cbfbe34" continuedAt="Text_497348934d334eaeb3b059bf54cbfbe35"><ix:continuation id="Text_c4d5dd92edac4e12aff80ee0dd02daa659" continuedAt="Text_c4d5dd92edac4e12aff80ee0dd02daa660">
<div style="text-align: justify; font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">For all loan classes within the Company&#8217;s loan portfolio, loans are placed on nonaccrual status when timely collection of principal and/or interest in accordance with
      contractual terms is in doubt. Loans are transferred to nonaccrual status generally when principal or interest payments become over <ix:nonNumeric name="nbtb:ThresholdPeriodPastDueForLoansToBeConsideredNonperforming" id="Fact_ea54b2a631044c119e72cfbcf181956a" contextRef="c20250101to20251231" format="ixt-sec:durwordsen">ninety days</ix:nonNumeric>
      delinquent, unless the loan is well secured and in the process of collection, or sooner when management concludes circumstances indicate that borrowers may be unable to meet contractual principal or interest payments.&#160;When a loan is transferred to a
      nonaccrual status, all interest previously accrued in the current period but not collected is reversed against interest income in that period. Interest accrued in a prior period and not collected is charged-off against the allowance for credit
      losses.</div>
</ix:continuation></ix:continuation>
    <ix:continuation id="Text_497348934d334eaeb3b059bf54cbfbe35" continuedAt="Text_497348934d334eaeb3b059bf54cbfbe36"><ix:continuation id="Text_c4d5dd92edac4e12aff80ee0dd02daa660" continuedAt="Text_c4d5dd92edac4e12aff80ee0dd02daa661">
<div><br/>
    </div>
</ix:continuation></ix:continuation>
    <ix:continuation id="Text_497348934d334eaeb3b059bf54cbfbe36" continuedAt="Text_497348934d334eaeb3b059bf54cbfbe37"><ix:continuation id="Text_c4d5dd92edac4e12aff80ee0dd02daa661" continuedAt="Text_c4d5dd92edac4e12aff80ee0dd02daa662">
<div style="text-align: justify; font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">If ultimate repayment of a nonaccrual loan is expected, any payments received are applied in accordance with contractual terms. If ultimate repayment of principal is not
      expected, any payment received on a nonaccrual loan is applied to principal until ultimate repayment becomes expected.&#160;For all loan classes within the Company&#8217;s loan portfolio, nonaccrual loans are returned to accrual status when they become current
      as to principal and interest and demonstrate a period of performance under the contractual terms and, in the opinion of management, are fully collectible as to principal and interest.&#160;For loans in all portfolios, the principal amount is charged off
      in full or in part as soon as management determines, based on available facts, that the collection of principal in full or in part is improbable.&#160;For Commercial loans, management considers specific facts and circumstances relative to individual
      credits in making such a determination. For Consumer and Residential loan classes, management uses specific guidance and thresholds from the Federal Financial Institutions Examination Council&#8217;s Uniform Retail Credit Classification and Account
      Management Policy.</div>
</ix:continuation></ix:continuation>
    <ix:continuation id="Text_497348934d334eaeb3b059bf54cbfbe37" continuedAt="Text_497348934d334eaeb3b059bf54cbfbe38"><ix:continuation id="Text_c4d5dd92edac4e12aff80ee0dd02daa662" continuedAt="Text_c4d5dd92edac4e12aff80ee0dd02daa663">
<div><br/>
    </div>
</ix:continuation></ix:continuation>
    <ix:continuation id="Text_497348934d334eaeb3b059bf54cbfbe38"><ix:continuation id="Text_c4d5dd92edac4e12aff80ee0dd02daa663" continuedAt="Text_c4d5dd92edac4e12aff80ee0dd02daa664">
<div style="text-align: justify; font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;"><span style="font-size: 10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman'; color: rgb(0, 0, 0);">Beginning in 2023, with the Company&#8217;s adoption of ASU <span style="font-style: italic;"><span style="font-style: normal;">2022-02,</span> Financial Instruments</span> - <span style="font-style: italic;">CECL Losses (Topic 326): Troubled Debt Restructurings and Vintage Disclosures <span style="font-style: normal;">(<span style="font-style: normal;">&#8220;</span>ASU 2022-02<span style="font-style: normal;">&#8221;</span>)</span></span><span style="font-style: normal;">, </span>the recognition of a</span> troubled debt restructuring (&#8220;TDR&#8221;)<span style="font-size: 10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman'; color: rgb(0, 0, 0);"> was eliminated and instead the Company evaluates borrowers who are experiencing financial difficulty or loan modifications to borrowers experiencing financial difficulties. When a borrower is
        experiencing financial difficulties and the Company modifies a loan, such modifications generally include one or a combination of the following: an extension of the maturity date at a stated rate of interest lower than the current market rate for
        new debt with similar risk; a change in scheduled payment amount; or principal forgiveness. Modifications to borrowers experiencing financial difficulty may be different from those previously disclosed in TDR disclosures since the Company is no
        longer required to determine if a concession has been granted, which was a requirement to determine whether a loan modification was considered to be a TDR. Historically, a TDR would generally include one or a combination of the following: an
        extension of the maturity date at a stated rate of interest lower than the current market rate for new debt with similar risk; a temporary reduction in the interest rate; or a change in scheduled payment amount. TDR loans were nonaccrual loans;
        however, they could be returned to accrual status after a period of performance, generally evidenced by <span style="font-size: 10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman'; color: rgb(0, 0, 0);"><ix:nonNumeric name="nbtb:PeriodOfSustainedRepaymentPerformanceForNonperformingTdrsToBeReturnedToPerformingStatus" id="Fact_154d0aecec044aeba3a09e89839a09ca" contextRef="c20250101to20251231" format="ixt-sec:durwordsen">six months</ix:nonNumeric></span> of compliance with their modified terms. </span></div>
</ix:continuation></ix:continuation>

    <ix:continuation id="Text_c4d5dd92edac4e12aff80ee0dd02daa664" continuedAt="Text_c4d5dd92edac4e12aff80ee0dd02daa665">
<div style="text-align: left;"><br/>
    </div>
</ix:continuation>

    <ix:nonNumeric name="us-gaap:CreditLossFinancialInstrumentPolicyTextBlock" id="Text_545140f3bc7f4f14be989f4d30bcf32c" contextRef="c20250101to20251231" escape="true" continuedAt="Text_6ad9441a9fba497ab039048ad6d1d7831"><ix:continuation id="Text_c4d5dd92edac4e12aff80ee0dd02daa665" continuedAt="Text_c4d5dd92edac4e12aff80ee0dd02daa666">
<div style="text-align: justify; color: rgb(0, 0, 0); font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; font-weight: bold;">Allowance for Credit Losses - Loans</div>
</ix:continuation></ix:nonNumeric>
    <ix:continuation id="Text_6ad9441a9fba497ab039048ad6d1d7831" continuedAt="Text_6ad9441a9fba497ab039048ad6d1d7832"><ix:continuation id="Text_c4d5dd92edac4e12aff80ee0dd02daa666" continuedAt="Text_c4d5dd92edac4e12aff80ee0dd02daa667">
<div><br/>
    </div>
</ix:continuation></ix:continuation>
    <ix:continuation id="Text_6ad9441a9fba497ab039048ad6d1d7832" continuedAt="Text_6ad9441a9fba497ab039048ad6d1d7833"><ix:continuation id="Text_c4d5dd92edac4e12aff80ee0dd02daa667" continuedAt="Text_c4d5dd92edac4e12aff80ee0dd02daa668">
<div style="text-align: justify; color: rgb(0, 0, 0); font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">The CECL methodology requires an estimate of the credit losses expected over the life of a loan (or pool of loans). The allowance for credit losses
      is a valuation account that is deducted from, or added to, the loans&#8217; amortized cost basis to present the net, lifetime amount expected to be collected on the loans. Loan losses are charged off against the allowance when management believes a loan
      balance is confirmed to be uncollectible. Expected recoveries do not exceed the aggregate of amounts previously charged-off and expected to be charged-off.</div>
</ix:continuation></ix:continuation>
    <ix:continuation id="Text_6ad9441a9fba497ab039048ad6d1d7833" continuedAt="Text_6ad9441a9fba497ab039048ad6d1d7834"><ix:continuation id="Text_c4d5dd92edac4e12aff80ee0dd02daa668" continuedAt="Text_c4d5dd92edac4e12aff80ee0dd02daa669">
<div><br/>
    </div>
</ix:continuation></ix:continuation>
    <ix:continuation id="Text_6ad9441a9fba497ab039048ad6d1d7834" continuedAt="Text_6ad9441a9fba497ab039048ad6d1d7835"><ix:continuation id="Text_c4d5dd92edac4e12aff80ee0dd02daa669" continuedAt="Text_c4d5dd92edac4e12aff80ee0dd02daa670">
<div style="text-align: justify; color: rgb(0, 0, 0); font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">Management estimates the allowance balance for credit losses using relevant information, from internal and external sources, related to past events,
      current conditions, and reasonable and supportable forecasts that affect the collectability of the reported amounts. Historical loss experience is generally the starting point for estimating expected credit losses. The Company then considers whether
      the historical loss experience should be adjusted for asset-specific risk characteristics or current conditions at the reporting date that did not exist over the period from which historical experience is used. Adjustments to historical loss
      information is made for differences in current loan-specific risk characteristics such as differences in underwriting standards, portfolio mix, delinquency level or term as well as changes in environmental conditions, such as changes in unemployment
      rates, production metrics, property values, or other relevant factors. Company historical loss experience is supplemented with peer information when there is insufficient loss data for the Company. Peer selection is based on a review of institutions
      with comparable loss experience as well as loan yield, bank size, portfolio concentration and geography. Finally, the Company considers forecasts about future economic conditions that are reasonable and supportable. Significant management judgment is
      required at various points in the measurement process.</div>
</ix:continuation></ix:continuation>
    <ix:continuation id="Text_6ad9441a9fba497ab039048ad6d1d7835" continuedAt="Text_6ad9441a9fba497ab039048ad6d1d7836"><ix:continuation id="Text_c4d5dd92edac4e12aff80ee0dd02daa670" continuedAt="Text_c4d5dd92edac4e12aff80ee0dd02daa671">
<div><br/>
    </div>
</ix:continuation></ix:continuation>
    <ix:continuation id="Text_6ad9441a9fba497ab039048ad6d1d7836" continuedAt="Text_6ad9441a9fba497ab039048ad6d1d7837"><ix:continuation id="Text_c4d5dd92edac4e12aff80ee0dd02daa671" continuedAt="Text_c4d5dd92edac4e12aff80ee0dd02daa672">
<div style="text-align: justify; color: rgb(0, 0, 0); font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">Portfolio segment is defined as the level at which an entity develops and documents a systematic methodology to determine its allowance for credit
      losses. Upon adoption of CECL, management revised the manner in which loans were pooled for similar risk characteristics. Management developed segments for estimating loss based on type of borrower and collateral which is generally based upon federal
      call report segmentation and have been combined or subsegmented as needed to ensure loans of similar risk profiles are appropriately pooled.</div>
</ix:continuation></ix:continuation>
    <ix:continuation id="Text_6ad9441a9fba497ab039048ad6d1d7837" continuedAt="Text_6ad9441a9fba497ab039048ad6d1d7838"><ix:continuation id="Text_c4d5dd92edac4e12aff80ee0dd02daa672" continuedAt="Text_c4d5dd92edac4e12aff80ee0dd02daa673">
<div><br/>
    </div>
</ix:continuation></ix:continuation>

<div style="text-align: justify; color: rgb(0, 0, 0); font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">The Company offers a variety of commercial loan products. The Company&#8217;s underwriting analysis for commercial loans typically includes credit
      verification, independent appraisals, a review of the borrower&#8217;s financial condition and a detailed analysis of the borrower&#8217;s underlying cash flows.</div>
</ix:continuation></ix:continuation>
    <ix:continuation id="Text_6ad9441a9fba497ab039048ad6d1d78315" continuedAt="Text_6ad9441a9fba497ab039048ad6d1d78316"><ix:continuation id="Text_c4d5dd92edac4e12aff80ee0dd02daa680" continuedAt="Text_c4d5dd92edac4e12aff80ee0dd02daa681">

<div style="text-align: justify; color: rgb(0, 0, 0); font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;"><span style="font-size: 10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-style: italic;">Commercial and Industrial (&#8220;C&amp;I&#8221;)</span> &#8211; The Company offers
      a variety of loan options to meet the specific needs of our C&amp;I customers including term loans, time notes and lines of credit. Such loans are made available to businesses for working capital needs and are typically collateralized by business
      assets such as equipment, accounts receivable and perishable agricultural products, which are exposed to industry price volatility. To reduce these risks, management also attempts to obtain personal guarantees of the owners or to obtain government
      loan guarantees to provide further support.</div>
</ix:continuation></ix:continuation>
    <ix:continuation id="Text_6ad9441a9fba497ab039048ad6d1d78317" continuedAt="Text_6ad9441a9fba497ab039048ad6d1d78318"><ix:continuation id="Text_c4d5dd92edac4e12aff80ee0dd02daa682" continuedAt="Text_c4d5dd92edac4e12aff80ee0dd02daa683">

<div style="text-align: justify; color: rgb(0, 0, 0); font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;"><span style="font-size: 10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-style: italic;">Commercial Real Estate (&#8220;CRE&#8221;)</span> &#8211; The Company offers CRE
      loans to finance real estate purchases, refinancing&#8217;s, expansions and improvements to commercial and agricultural properties. CRE loans are loans that are secured by liens on real estate, which may include both owner-occupied and nonowner-occupied
      properties, such as apartments, commercial structures, health care facilities and other facilities. The Company&#8217;s underwriting analysis includes credit verification, independent appraisals, a review of the borrower&#8217;s financial condition and a
      detailed analysis of the borrower&#8217;s underlying cash flows. These loans are typically originated in amounts of no more than <ix:nonFraction name="nbtb:LoanOriginationAmountPercentageOfAppraisedValueOrPurchasePriceOfProperty" id="Fact_732d13d5258445aaa853463a58892197" contextRef="c20251231_FinancingReceivablePortfolioSegmentAxis_CommercialPortfolioSegmentMember_FinancingReceivableRecordedInvestmentByClassOfFinancingReceivableAxis_RealEstateLoanMember_RangeAxis_MaximumMember" unitRef="U005" decimals="2" scale="-2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal">80</ix:nonFraction>% of the
      appraised value of the property. Government loan guarantees may be obtained to provide further support for agricultural property.</div>
</ix:continuation></ix:continuation>

<div style="text-align: justify; color: rgb(0, 0, 0); font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; font-weight: bold;"><span style="text-decoration: underline;">Consumer Loans</span></div>
</ix:continuation></ix:continuation>
    <ix:continuation id="Text_6ad9441a9fba497ab039048ad6d1d78321" continuedAt="Text_6ad9441a9fba497ab039048ad6d1d78322"><ix:continuation id="Text_c4d5dd92edac4e12aff80ee0dd02daa686" continuedAt="Text_c4d5dd92edac4e12aff80ee0dd02daa687">

    <ix:continuation id="Text_6ad9441a9fba497ab039048ad6d1d78322" continuedAt="Text_6ad9441a9fba497ab039048ad6d1d78323"><ix:continuation id="Text_c4d5dd92edac4e12aff80ee0dd02daa687" continuedAt="Text_c4d5dd92edac4e12aff80ee0dd02daa688">
<div style="text-align: justify; color: rgb(0, 0, 0); font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">The Company offers a variety of Consumer loan products including Auto, Residential Solar and Other Consumer loans.</div>
</ix:continuation></ix:continuation>
    <ix:continuation id="Text_6ad9441a9fba497ab039048ad6d1d78323" continuedAt="Text_6ad9441a9fba497ab039048ad6d1d78324"><ix:continuation id="Text_c4d5dd92edac4e12aff80ee0dd02daa688" continuedAt="Text_c4d5dd92edac4e12aff80ee0dd02daa689">
<div><br/>
    </div>
</ix:continuation></ix:continuation>
    <ix:continuation id="Text_6ad9441a9fba497ab039048ad6d1d78324" continuedAt="Text_6ad9441a9fba497ab039048ad6d1d78325"><ix:continuation id="Text_c4d5dd92edac4e12aff80ee0dd02daa689" continuedAt="Text_c4d5dd92edac4e12aff80ee0dd02daa690">
<div style="text-align: justify; color: rgb(0, 0, 0); font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;"><span style="font-size: 10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-style: italic;">Auto </span>&#8211; The Company provides both direct and indirect
      financing of automobiles (&#8220;Auto&#8221;). The Company maintains relationships with a wide network of dealers throughout the areas we serve across the northeastern United States. Through these relationships, the Company primarily finances the purchases of
      automobiles indirectly through dealer relationships. Auto loans are secured with collateral consisting of a perfected lien on the vehicle being purchased. Most of these loans carry a fixed rate of interest with principal repayment terms typically
      ranging from <span style="-sec-ix-hidden:Fact_b0988f126a644e9a92ae080c4785cddc">three</span> to <ix:nonNumeric name="nbtb:FinancingReceivablePrincipalRepaymentTerm" id="Fact_5e358ed4397d4f3ea0e249013b26044b" contextRef="c20250101to20251231_FinancingReceivablePortfolioSegmentAxis_ConsumerPortfolioSegmentMember_FinancingReceivableRecordedInvestmentByClassOfFinancingReceivableAxis_AutoFinancingReceivableMember_RangeAxis_MaximumMember" format="ixt-sec:durwordsen">seven years</ix:nonNumeric>,
      based upon the nature of the collateral and the size of the loan.</div>
</ix:continuation></ix:continuation>
    <ix:continuation id="Text_6ad9441a9fba497ab039048ad6d1d78325" continuedAt="Text_6ad9441a9fba497ab039048ad6d1d78326"><ix:continuation id="Text_c4d5dd92edac4e12aff80ee0dd02daa690" continuedAt="Text_c4d5dd92edac4e12aff80ee0dd02daa691">
<div style="text-align: justify; color: rgb(0, 0, 0); font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;"> <br/>
    </div>
</ix:continuation></ix:continuation>
    <ix:continuation id="Text_6ad9441a9fba497ab039048ad6d1d78326" continuedAt="Text_6ad9441a9fba497ab039048ad6d1d78327"><ix:continuation id="Text_c4d5dd92edac4e12aff80ee0dd02daa691" continuedAt="Text_c4d5dd92edac4e12aff80ee0dd02daa692">
<div style="text-align: justify;"><span style="font-style: italic; background-color: rgb(255, 255, 255); font-weight: normal; color: rgb(0, 0, 0); font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; text-transform: none;">Residential
        Solar</span><span style="background-color: rgb(255, 255, 255); font-weight: normal; color: rgb(0, 0, 0); font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; text-transform: none;"> &#8211; The Company previously offered loans across a
        national footprint originated through our relationships with national technology-driven consumer lending companies to finance the purchase and installation of residential solar energy. Advances of credit through this business line are subject to
        the Company&#8217;s underwriting standards including criteria such as FICO score and debt to income thresholds. In 2017, the Company partnered with Sungage Financial, LLC. to offer financing to consumers for solar ownership with the program tailored for
        delivery through solar installers. Advances of credit through this business line are to prime borrowers and are subject to the Company&#8217;s underwriting standards. Residential solar loans carry a fixed rate of interest with principal repayment terms
        typically ranging from <span style="-sec-ix-hidden:Fact_c2b5607f09ba48d9bfca4e17709e49a6">five</span> to <ix:nonNumeric name="nbtb:FinancingReceivablePrincipalRepaymentTerm" id="Fact_ebb338d8d2894b5b9dd615fc404bec9f" contextRef="c20250101to20251231_FinancingReceivablePortfolioSegmentAxis_ConsumerPortfolioSegmentMember_FinancingReceivableRecordedInvestmentByClassOfFinancingReceivableAxis_ResidentialSolarMember_RangeAxis_MaximumMember" format="ixt-sec:durwordsen">twenty-five years</ix:nonNumeric>. Typically, the Company collects origination fees that are deferred and recognized into interest income over the estimated life of the loan.</span><br/>
    </div>
</ix:continuation></ix:continuation>
    <ix:continuation id="Text_6ad9441a9fba497ab039048ad6d1d78327" continuedAt="Text_6ad9441a9fba497ab039048ad6d1d78328"><ix:continuation id="Text_c4d5dd92edac4e12aff80ee0dd02daa692" continuedAt="Text_c4d5dd92edac4e12aff80ee0dd02daa693">
<div><br/></div>
</ix:continuation></ix:continuation>
    <div>
      <ix:continuation id="Text_6ad9441a9fba497ab039048ad6d1d78328" continuedAt="Text_6ad9441a9fba497ab039048ad6d1d78329"><ix:continuation id="Text_c4d5dd92edac4e12aff80ee0dd02daa693" continuedAt="Text_c4d5dd92edac4e12aff80ee0dd02daa694">
<div style="text-align: justify; color: rgb(0, 0, 0); font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;"><span style="font-size: 10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-style: italic;">Other Consumer</span><span style="font-size: 10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman';">&#160;&#8211; The Other Consumer loan segment consists primarily of unsecured consumer loans and direct consumer loans. The Company offers a variety of direct consumer installment loans to finance various personal expenditures. In
          addition to installment loans, the Company also offers personal lines of credit, overdraft protection, debt consolidation, education and other uses. Direct consumer installment loans carry a fixed rate of interest with principal repayment terms
          typically ranging from <span style="-sec-ix-hidden:Fact_31d8de3fb1304d7da791de7b23f3434f">one</span> to <ix:nonNumeric name="nbtb:FinancingReceivablePrincipalRepaymentTerm" id="Fact_2a982ebbd14c468d9ae76919c452ec7a" contextRef="c20250101to20251231_FinancingReceivablePortfolioSegmentAxis_ConsumerPortfolioSegmentMember_FinancingReceivableRecordedInvestmentByClassOfFinancingReceivableAxis_InstallmentFinancingReceivableMember_RangeAxis_MaximumMember" format="ixt-sec:durwordsen">fifteen years</ix:nonNumeric>, based upon the nature of the collateral and the size of the loan. Consumer installment loans are often secured with collateral consisting of a perfected lien on the asset being purchased or a perfected lien on a
          consumer&#8217;s deposit account. Risk is reduced through underwriting criteria, which include credit verification, appraisals, a review of the borrower&#8217;s financial condition and personal cash flows. A security interest, with title insurance when
          necessary, is taken in the underlying real estate. The Company previously offered unsecured consumer loans across a national footprint originated through our relationships with national technology-driven consumer lending companies to finance such
          things as dental and medical procedures, K-12 tuition and other consumer purpose loans. Advances of credit through this business line were subject to the Company&#8217;s underwriting standards including criteria such as FICO score and debt to income
          thresholds. Advances of credit through this business line were to prime borrowers and are subject to the Company&#8217;s underwriting standards. Typically, the Company collects origination fees that are deferred and recognized into interest income over
          the estimated life of the loan.</span></div>
</ix:continuation></ix:continuation>
    </div>

    <ix:continuation id="Text_6ad9441a9fba497ab039048ad6d1d78329" continuedAt="Text_6ad9441a9fba497ab039048ad6d1d78330"><ix:continuation id="Text_c4d5dd92edac4e12aff80ee0dd02daa694" continuedAt="Text_c4d5dd92edac4e12aff80ee0dd02daa695">
<div><br/>
    </div>

      <div style="text-align: center;" class="BRPFPageNumberArea"><span style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif; font-size: 8pt; font-weight: normal; font-style: normal;">62</span></div>

    <ix:continuation id="Text_6ad9441a9fba497ab039048ad6d1d78330" continuedAt="Text_6ad9441a9fba497ab039048ad6d1d78331"><ix:continuation id="Text_c4d5dd92edac4e12aff80ee0dd02daa695" continuedAt="Text_c4d5dd92edac4e12aff80ee0dd02daa696">
<div style="text-align: justify; color: rgb(0, 0, 0); font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; font-weight: bold;"><span style="text-decoration: underline;">Residential</span></div>
</ix:continuation></ix:continuation>
    <ix:continuation id="Text_6ad9441a9fba497ab039048ad6d1d78331" continuedAt="Text_6ad9441a9fba497ab039048ad6d1d78332"><ix:continuation id="Text_c4d5dd92edac4e12aff80ee0dd02daa696" continuedAt="Text_c4d5dd92edac4e12aff80ee0dd02daa697">
<div><br/>
    </div>
</ix:continuation></ix:continuation>
    <ix:continuation id="Text_6ad9441a9fba497ab039048ad6d1d78332" continuedAt="Text_6ad9441a9fba497ab039048ad6d1d78333"><ix:continuation id="Text_c4d5dd92edac4e12aff80ee0dd02daa697" continuedAt="Text_c4d5dd92edac4e12aff80ee0dd02daa698">
<div style="text-align: justify; color: rgb(0, 0, 0); font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">Residential loans consist primarily of loans secured by a first or second mortgage on primary residences, home equity loans and lines of credit in
      first and second lien positions and residential construction loans. We originate adjustable-rate and fixed rate, one-to-four-family residential loans for the construction or purchase of a residential property or the refinancing of a mortgage. These
      loans are collateralized by properties located in the Company&#8217;s market area. Loans on one-to-four-family residential are generally originated in amounts of no more than <ix:nonFraction name="nbtb:LoanOriginationAmountPercentageOfAppraisedValueOrPurchasePriceOfProperty" id="Fact_37c544e959ae445aa5f71750c3eb0afc" contextRef="c20251231_FinancingReceivablePortfolioSegmentAxis_ResidentialPortfolioSegmentMember_RangeAxis_MaximumMember" unitRef="U005" decimals="2" scale="-2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal">85</ix:nonFraction>% of the purchase price or appraised value (whichever is lower) or have private mortgage insurance. Mortgage title insurance and hazard insurance are normally required. Construction loans have a unique risk because
      they are secured by an incomplete dwelling. This risk is reduced through periodic site inspections, including one at each loan draw period. For home equity loans, consumers are able to borrow up to <ix:nonFraction name="nbtb:LoanOriginationAmountPercentageOfEquityInProperty" id="Fact_90eb8056d1f74748a87ddcc5e317e9c0" contextRef="c20251231_FinancingReceivablePortfolioSegmentAxis_ResidentialPortfolioSegmentMember_FinancingReceivableRecordedInvestmentByClassOfFinancingReceivableAxis_HomeEquityFinancingReceivablesMember_RangeAxis_MaximumMember" unitRef="U005" decimals="2" scale="-2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal">85</ix:nonFraction>% of the equity in their homes and are generally tied to Prime with a <ix:nonNumeric name="nbtb:FinancingReceivableTermOfDraw" id="Fact_43226811aec4428b849c527eaef97083" contextRef="c20250101to20251231_FinancingReceivablePortfolioSegmentAxis_ResidentialPortfolioSegmentMember_FinancingReceivableRecordedInvestmentByClassOfFinancingReceivableAxis_HomeEquityFinancingReceivablesMember_RangeAxis_MaximumMember" format="ixt-sec:durwordsen">ten-year</ix:nonNumeric>
      draw followed by a <ix:nonNumeric name="nbtb:FinancingReceivableAmortizationTerm" id="Fact_7d3ec15afe5d4150a0506384ad2ee2cf" contextRef="c20250101to20251231_FinancingReceivablePortfolioSegmentAxis_ResidentialPortfolioSegmentMember_FinancingReceivableRecordedInvestmentByClassOfFinancingReceivableAxis_HomeEquityFinancingReceivablesMember_RangeAxis_MaximumMember" format="ixt-sec:durwordsen">fifteen-year</ix:nonNumeric> amortization. These loans carry a higher risk than first mortgage residential loans as they are often in a
      second position with respect to collateral.</div>
</ix:continuation></ix:continuation>
    <ix:continuation id="Text_6ad9441a9fba497ab039048ad6d1d78333" continuedAt="Text_6ad9441a9fba497ab039048ad6d1d78334"><ix:continuation id="Text_c4d5dd92edac4e12aff80ee0dd02daa698" continuedAt="Text_c4d5dd92edac4e12aff80ee0dd02daa699">
<div><br/>
    </div>
</ix:continuation></ix:continuation>
    <ix:continuation id="Text_6ad9441a9fba497ab039048ad6d1d78334" continuedAt="Text_6ad9441a9fba497ab039048ad6d1d78335"><ix:continuation id="Text_c4d5dd92edac4e12aff80ee0dd02daa699" continuedAt="Text_c4d5dd92edac4e12aff80ee0dd02daa6100">
<div style="text-align: justify; color: rgb(0, 0, 0); font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">Historical credit loss experience over the observation period for both the Company and segment-specific peers provides the basis for the estimation
      of expected credit losses, where observed credit losses are converted using models to probability of default (&#8220;PD&#8221;) rate curves through the use of segment-specific loss given default (&#8220;LGD&#8221;) risk factors that convert default rates to loss severity
      based on industry-level, observed relationships between the two variables for each asset class, primarily due to the nature of the underlying collateral. These risk factors were assessed for reasonableness against the Company&#8217;s own loss experience
      and adjusted in certain cases when the relationship between the Company&#8217;s historical default and loss severity deviated from that of the wider industry. The historical PD curves, together with corresponding economic conditions, establish a
      quantitative relationship between economic conditions and loan performance through an economic cycle.</div>
</ix:continuation></ix:continuation>
    <ix:continuation id="Text_6ad9441a9fba497ab039048ad6d1d78335" continuedAt="Text_6ad9441a9fba497ab039048ad6d1d78336"><ix:continuation id="Text_c4d5dd92edac4e12aff80ee0dd02daa6100" continuedAt="Text_c4d5dd92edac4e12aff80ee0dd02daa6101">
<div><br/>
    </div>
</ix:continuation></ix:continuation>
    <ix:continuation id="Text_6ad9441a9fba497ab039048ad6d1d78336" continuedAt="Text_6ad9441a9fba497ab039048ad6d1d78337"><ix:continuation id="Text_c4d5dd92edac4e12aff80ee0dd02daa6101" continuedAt="Text_c4d5dd92edac4e12aff80ee0dd02daa6102">
<div style="text-align: justify; color: rgb(0, 0, 0); font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">Using the historical relationship between economic conditions and loan performance, management&#8217;s expectation of future loan performance is
      incorporated using externally developed economic forecasts which are probabilistically weighted to reflect potential forecast inaccuracy and model limitations. These forecasts are applied over a period that management has determined to be reasonable
      and supportable. Beyond the period over which management can develop or source a reasonable and supportable forecast, the model will revert to long-term average economic conditions using a straight-line, time-based methodology.</div>
</ix:continuation></ix:continuation>
    <ix:continuation id="Text_6ad9441a9fba497ab039048ad6d1d78337" continuedAt="Text_6ad9441a9fba497ab039048ad6d1d78338"><ix:continuation id="Text_c4d5dd92edac4e12aff80ee0dd02daa6102" continuedAt="Text_c4d5dd92edac4e12aff80ee0dd02daa6103">
<div><br/>
    </div>
</ix:continuation></ix:continuation>
    <ix:continuation id="Text_6ad9441a9fba497ab039048ad6d1d78338" continuedAt="Text_6ad9441a9fba497ab039048ad6d1d78339"><ix:continuation id="Text_c4d5dd92edac4e12aff80ee0dd02daa6103" continuedAt="Text_c4d5dd92edac4e12aff80ee0dd02daa6104">
<div style="text-align: justify; color: rgb(0, 0, 0); font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">The allowance for credit losses is measured on a collective (pool) basis, with both a quantitative and qualitative analysis that is applied on a
      quarterly basis, when similar risk characteristics exist. The respective quantitative allowance for each segment is measured using an econometric, PD/LGD modeling methodology in which distinct, segment-specific multi-variate regression models are
      applied to multiple, probabilistically weighted external economic forecasts of economic variables. Under the discounted cash flows methodology, expected credit losses are estimated over the effective life of the loans by measuring the difference
      between the net present value of modeled cash flows and amortized cost basis. Contractual cash flows over the contractual life of the loans are the basis for modeled cash flows, adjusted for modeled defaults, expected prepayments and curtailments and
      discounted at the loan-level stated interest rate. The contractual term excludes expected extensions, renewals, and modifications unless the extension or renewal options are included in the original or modified contract at the reporting date and are
      not unconditionally cancellable by the Company.</div>
</ix:continuation></ix:continuation>
    <ix:continuation id="Text_6ad9441a9fba497ab039048ad6d1d78339" continuedAt="Text_6ad9441a9fba497ab039048ad6d1d78340"><ix:continuation id="Text_c4d5dd92edac4e12aff80ee0dd02daa6104" continuedAt="Text_c4d5dd92edac4e12aff80ee0dd02daa6105">
<div><br/>
    </div>
</ix:continuation></ix:continuation>
    <ix:continuation id="Text_6ad9441a9fba497ab039048ad6d1d78340" continuedAt="Text_6ad9441a9fba497ab039048ad6d1d78341"><ix:continuation id="Text_c4d5dd92edac4e12aff80ee0dd02daa6105" continuedAt="Text_c4d5dd92edac4e12aff80ee0dd02daa6106">
<div style="text-align: justify; color: rgb(0, 0, 0); font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">After quantitative considerations, management applies additional qualitative adjustments so that the allowance for credit losses is reflective of
      the estimate of lifetime losses that exist in the loan portfolio at the balance sheet date. Qualitative considerations include limitations inherent in the quantitative model; trends experienced in nonperforming and delinquent loans; changes in value
      of underlying collateral; changes in lending policies and procedures; nature and composition of loans; portfolio concentrations that may affect loss experience across one or more components of the portfolio; the experience, ability and depth of
      lending management and staff; the Company&#8217;s credit review system; and the effect of external factors; such as competition, legal and regulatory requirements.</div>
</ix:continuation></ix:continuation>
    <ix:continuation id="Text_6ad9441a9fba497ab039048ad6d1d78341" continuedAt="Text_6ad9441a9fba497ab039048ad6d1d78342"><ix:continuation id="Text_c4d5dd92edac4e12aff80ee0dd02daa6106" continuedAt="Text_c4d5dd92edac4e12aff80ee0dd02daa6107">
<div><br/></div>
</ix:continuation></ix:continuation>
    <ix:continuation id="Text_6ad9441a9fba497ab039048ad6d1d78342" continuedAt="Text_6ad9441a9fba497ab039048ad6d1d78343"><ix:continuation id="Text_c4d5dd92edac4e12aff80ee0dd02daa6107" continuedAt="Text_c4d5dd92edac4e12aff80ee0dd02daa6108">
<div style="text-align: justify; color: rgb(0, 0, 0); font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">The threshold for evaluating commercial loans risk graded substandard or doubtful, and nonperforming loans specifically evaluated for individual
      credit loss is $<ix:nonFraction name="nbtb:FinancingReceivableThresholdBalanceForLoansSpecificallyEvaluatedForIndividualCreditLoss" id="Fact_21d0d6f61ea24313badc57831aa9fb8f" contextRef="c20251231_RangeAxis_MinimumMember" unitRef="U001" decimals="-5" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal">1.0</ix:nonFraction> million. When management determines that foreclosure is probable, expected credit losses are based on the fair value of
      the collateral at the reporting date, adjusted for selling costs as appropriate. If the loan is not collateral dependent, the allowance for credit losses related to individually assessed loans is based on discounted expected cash flows using the
      loan&#8217;s initial effective interest rate. Generally, individually assessed loans are collateral dependent.</div>
</ix:continuation></ix:continuation>
    <ix:continuation id="Text_6ad9441a9fba497ab039048ad6d1d78343" continuedAt="Text_6ad9441a9fba497ab039048ad6d1d78344"><ix:continuation id="Text_c4d5dd92edac4e12aff80ee0dd02daa6108" continuedAt="Text_c4d5dd92edac4e12aff80ee0dd02daa6109">
<div><br/>
    </div>
</ix:continuation></ix:continuation>
    <div style="clear: both; margin-top: 10pt; margin-bottom: 10pt;" class="BRPFPageBreakArea">
      <div style="text-align: center;" class="BRPFPageNumberArea"><span style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif; font-size: 8pt; font-weight: normal; font-style: normal;">63</span></div>

    <ix:continuation id="Text_6ad9441a9fba497ab039048ad6d1d78344" continuedAt="Text_6ad9441a9fba497ab039048ad6d1d78345"><ix:continuation id="Text_c4d5dd92edac4e12aff80ee0dd02daa6109" continuedAt="Text_c4d5dd92edac4e12aff80ee0dd02daa6110">
<div style="text-align: justify; color: rgb(0, 0, 0); font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; font-style: italic;">Allowance for Credit Losses on Off-Balance Sheet Credit Exposures</div>
</ix:continuation></ix:continuation>
    <ix:continuation id="Text_6ad9441a9fba497ab039048ad6d1d78345" continuedAt="Text_6ad9441a9fba497ab039048ad6d1d78346"><ix:continuation id="Text_c4d5dd92edac4e12aff80ee0dd02daa6110" continuedAt="Text_c4d5dd92edac4e12aff80ee0dd02daa6111">
<div><br/>
    </div>
</ix:continuation></ix:continuation>
    <ix:continuation id="Text_6ad9441a9fba497ab039048ad6d1d78346" continuedAt="Text_6ad9441a9fba497ab039048ad6d1d78347"><ix:continuation id="Text_c4d5dd92edac4e12aff80ee0dd02daa6111" continuedAt="Text_c4d5dd92edac4e12aff80ee0dd02daa6112">
<div style="text-align: justify; color: rgb(0, 0, 0); font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">The Company estimates expected credit losses over the contractual period in which the Company has exposure to credit risk via a contractual
      obligation to extend credit, unless that obligation is unconditionally cancellable by the Company. The allowance for credit losses on off-balance sheet credit exposures is adjusted as an expense in other noninterest expense. The estimate includes
      consideration of the likelihood that funding will occur and an estimate of expected credit losses on commitments expected to be funded over their estimated lives. Estimating credit losses on unfunded commitments requires the Bank to consider the
      following categories of off-balance sheet credit exposure: unfunded commitments to extend credit, unfunded lines of credit and standby letters of credit. Each of these unfunded commitments is then analyzed for a probability of funding to calculate a
      probable funding amount. The life of loan loss factor by related portfolio segment from the loan allowance for credit loss calculation is then applied to the probable funding amount to calculate a reserve on unfunded commitments.</div>
</ix:continuation></ix:continuation>
    <ix:continuation id="Text_6ad9441a9fba497ab039048ad6d1d78347" continuedAt="Text_6ad9441a9fba497ab039048ad6d1d78348"><ix:continuation id="Text_c4d5dd92edac4e12aff80ee0dd02daa6112" continuedAt="Text_c4d5dd92edac4e12aff80ee0dd02daa6113">
<div><br/>
    </div>
</ix:continuation></ix:continuation>
    <ix:continuation id="Text_6ad9441a9fba497ab039048ad6d1d78348" continuedAt="Text_6ad9441a9fba497ab039048ad6d1d78349"><ix:continuation id="Text_c4d5dd92edac4e12aff80ee0dd02daa6113" continuedAt="Text_c4d5dd92edac4e12aff80ee0dd02daa6114">
<div style="text-align: justify; color: rgb(0, 0, 0); font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; font-style: italic;">Accrued Interest Receivable</div>
</ix:continuation></ix:continuation>
    <ix:continuation id="Text_6ad9441a9fba497ab039048ad6d1d78349" continuedAt="Text_6ad9441a9fba497ab039048ad6d1d78350"><ix:continuation id="Text_c4d5dd92edac4e12aff80ee0dd02daa6114" continuedAt="Text_c4d5dd92edac4e12aff80ee0dd02daa6115">
