<div style="text-align: justify; color: rgb(0, 0, 0); font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">The acquisitions of Evans and Salisbury are being accounted for as business combinations<span style="color: rgb(0, 0, 0); font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; font-style: normal; font-variant-ligatures: normal; font-variant-caps: normal; font-weight: 400; letter-spacing: normal; text-align: justify; text-indent: 0px; text-transform: none; word-spacing: 0px; white-space: normal; background-color: rgb(255, 255, 255); text-decoration-style: initial; text-decoration-color: initial; display: inline ! important; float: none;"> in accordance with ASC 805, &#8220;Business Combinations&#8221; (&#8220;ASC 805&#8221;), using the acquisition method of
        accounting. Accordingly, as of the date of the acquisition, the Company recorded the assets acquired, liabilities assumed and consideration paid at fair value based on management&#8217;s best estimates using information available at the date of the
        acquisition. These estimates were subject to adjustment based on updated information not available at the time of the acquisition and all amounts have now been finalized. The amount of goodwill arising from the acquisition consists largely of the
        synergies and economies of scale expected from combining the operations of the Company with Evans and Salisbury.</span><span style="font-size: 10pt;"> </span></div>
</ix:continuation>

<div style="color: rgb(0, 0, 0); font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;"> <span style="color: rgb(0, 0, 0); font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; font-style: normal; font-variant: normal; font-weight: normal; letter-spacing: normal; text-indent: 0px; text-transform: none; word-spacing: 0px; white-space: normal; background-color: rgb(255, 255, 255); text-decoration-style: initial; text-decoration-color: initial; display: inline ! important; float: none;">The following
          is a description of the valuation methodologies used to estimate the fair values of major categories of assets acquired and liabilities assumed. The Company used an independent valuation specialist to assist with the determination of fair values
          for certain acquired assets and assumed liabilities.</span></div>
</ix:continuation>
      <ix:continuation id="Text_8897f296866c4b8b977c24fde419265918" continuedAt="Text_8897f296866c4b8b977c24fde419265919">
<div style="color: rgb(0, 0, 0); font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;"><span style="color: rgb(0, 0, 0); font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; font-style: normal; font-variant: normal; font-weight: normal; letter-spacing: normal; text-indent: 0px; text-transform: none; word-spacing: 0px; white-space: normal; background-color: rgb(255, 255, 255); text-decoration-style: initial; text-decoration-color: initial; display: inline ! important; float: none;"> <br/>
        </span></div>
</ix:continuation>
      <ix:continuation id="Text_8897f296866c4b8b977c24fde419265919" continuedAt="Text_8897f296866c4b8b977c24fde419265920">
<div style="color: rgb(0, 0, 0); font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;"><span style="color: rgb(0, 0, 0); font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; font-style: normal; font-variant: normal; font-weight: normal; letter-spacing: normal; text-indent: 0px; text-transform: none; word-spacing: 0px; white-space: normal; background-color: rgb(255, 255, 255); text-decoration-style: initial; text-decoration-color: initial; display: inline ! important; float: none;"><span style="font-style: italic;">Cash and due from banks</span> - The estimated fair value was determined to approximate the carrying amount of these assets.</span> </div>
</ix:continuation>
      <ix:continuation id="Text_8897f296866c4b8b977c24fde419265920" continuedAt="Text_8897f296866c4b8b977c24fde419265921">
<div style="color: rgb(0, 0, 0); font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;"><span style="color: rgb(0, 0, 0); font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; font-style: normal; font-variant: normal; font-weight: normal; letter-spacing: normal; text-indent: 0px; text-transform: none; word-spacing: 0px; white-space: normal; background-color: rgb(255, 255, 255); text-decoration-style: initial; text-decoration-color: initial; display: inline ! important; float: none;"> <br/>
        </span></div>
</ix:continuation>
      <ix:continuation id="Text_8897f296866c4b8b977c24fde419265921" continuedAt="Text_8897f296866c4b8b977c24fde419265922">
<div style="color: rgb(0, 0, 0); font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;"><span style="color: rgb(0, 0, 0); font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; font-style: normal; font-variant: normal; font-weight: normal; letter-spacing: normal; text-indent: 0px; text-transform: none; word-spacing: 0px; white-space: normal; background-color: rgb(255, 255, 255); text-decoration-style: initial; text-decoration-color: initial; display: inline ! important; float: none;"> <span style="font-style: italic;">Securities available for sale</span> - The estimated fair value of the AFS investment portfolio was primarily determined using quoted market prices and dealer quotes. The investment securities were sold immediately
          after the merger and no gains or losses were recorded.</span></div>
</ix:continuation>
      <ix:continuation id="Text_8897f296866c4b8b977c24fde419265922" continuedAt="Text_8897f296866c4b8b977c24fde419265923">
<div style="color: rgb(0, 0, 0); font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;"><span style="color: rgb(0, 0, 0); font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; font-style: normal; font-variant: normal; font-weight: normal; letter-spacing: normal; text-indent: 0px; text-transform: none; word-spacing: 0px; white-space: normal; background-color: rgb(255, 255, 255); text-decoration-style: initial; text-decoration-color: initial; display: inline ! important; float: none;"> <br/>
        </span></div>
</ix:continuation>
      <div style="color: rgb(0, 0, 0); font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">
        <ix:continuation id="Text_8897f296866c4b8b977c24fde419265923" continuedAt="Text_8897f296866c4b8b977c24fde419265924">
<div style="display:none;"><br/></div>
<div style="color: rgb(0, 0, 0); font-family: 'Times New Roman',Times,serif; font-size: 13.3333px; font-style: normal; font-variant-ligatures: normal; font-variant-caps: normal; font-weight: 400; letter-spacing: normal; text-indent: 0px; text-transform: none; word-spacing: 0px; white-space: normal; background-color: rgb(255, 255, 255); text-decoration-style: initial; text-decoration-color: initial;"><span style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-style: italic; background-color: rgb(255, 255, 255); font-weight: normal; color: rgb(0, 0, 0); font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; text-transform: none;">Securities held to maturity&#160;<span style="font-style: italic;">-</span> <span style="font-style: normal;">The estimated fair value of the HTM investment portfolio, which consisted of local municipal securities, was retained at par, which is estimated to be equal to fair value.</span></span></div>
</ix:continuation><ix:continuation id="Text_8897f296866c4b8b977c24fde419265924" continuedAt="Text_8897f296866c4b8b977c24fde419265925">
<div><br class="Apple-interchange-newline"/>

        <span style="color: rgb(0, 0, 0); font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; font-style: normal; font-variant: normal; font-weight: normal; letter-spacing: normal; text-indent: 0px; text-transform: none; word-spacing: 0px; white-space: normal; background-color: rgb(255, 255, 255); text-decoration-style: initial; text-decoration-color: initial; display: inline ! important; float: none;"> </span></div>
</ix:continuation></div>

      <ix:continuation id="Text_8897f296866c4b8b977c24fde419265925" continuedAt="Text_8897f296866c4b8b977c24fde419265926">
<div style="color: rgb(0, 0, 0); font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;"><span style="color: rgb(0, 0, 0); font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; font-style: normal; font-variant: normal; font-weight: normal; letter-spacing: normal; text-indent: 0px; text-transform: none; word-spacing: 0px; white-space: normal; background-color: rgb(255, 255, 255); text-decoration-style: initial; text-decoration-color: initial; display: inline ! important; float: none;"><span style="font-style: italic;">Loans</span> - The </span><span style="color: rgb(0, 0, 0); font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; font-style: normal; font-variant-ligatures: normal; font-variant-caps: normal; font-weight: 400; letter-spacing: normal; text-indent: 0px; text-transform: none; word-spacing: 0px; white-space: normal; background-color: rgb(255, 255, 255); text-decoration-style: initial; text-decoration-color: initial; display: inline ! important; float: none;">estimated fair value of loans were based on a discounted cash flow methodology applied on a pooled basis. Loans were first segmented by purchased credit deteriorated (&#8220;PCD&#8221;) or non-purchased credit deteriorated (&#8220;non-PCD&#8221;) status, and then
          further grouped according to Federal Deposit Insurance Corporation (&#8220;FDIC&#8221;) call report segmentation. The valuation considered key loan characteristics including loan type, term, rate, payment schedule and loan performance attributes. Certain key
          assumptions related to prepayment speeds, PD, LGD and discount rate were also considered. The discount rates applied were based on a build-up approach factoring in the funding mix, servicing costs, liquidity premium and factors related to
          performance risk.</span><span style="color: rgb(0, 0, 0); font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; font-style: normal; font-variant: normal; font-weight: normal; letter-spacing: normal; text-indent: 0px; text-transform: none; word-spacing: 0px; white-space: normal; background-color: rgb(255, 255, 255); text-decoration-style: initial; text-decoration-color: initial; display: inline ! important; float: none;"> </span></div>
</ix:continuation>
      <ix:continuation id="Text_8897f296866c4b8b977c24fde419265926" continuedAt="Text_8897f296866c4b8b977c24fde419265927">
<div style="color: rgb(0, 0, 0); font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;"><span style="color: rgb(0, 0, 0); font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; font-style: normal; font-variant: normal; font-weight: normal; letter-spacing: normal; text-indent: 0px; text-transform: none; word-spacing: 0px; white-space: normal; background-color: rgb(255, 255, 255); text-decoration-style: initial; text-decoration-color: initial; display: inline ! important; float: none;"> <br/>
        </span></div>
</ix:continuation>
      <ix:continuation id="Text_8897f296866c4b8b977c24fde419265927" continuedAt="Text_8897f296866c4b8b977c24fde419265928">
<div style="color: rgb(0, 0, 0); font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;"><span style="color: rgb(0, 0, 0); font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; font-style: normal; font-variant: normal; font-weight: normal; letter-spacing: normal; text-indent: 0px; text-transform: none; word-spacing: 0px; white-space: normal; background-color: rgb(255, 255, 255); text-decoration-style: initial; text-decoration-color: initial; display: inline ! important; float: none;"> <span style="font-style: italic;">Core deposit intangible</span> - The core deposit intangible was valued utilizing the cost savings method approach, which recognizes the cost savings represented by the expense of maintaining the core deposit base
          versus the cost of an alternative funding source. The valuation incorporated assumptions related to account retention, discount rates, deposit interest rates, deposit maintenance costs and alternative funding rates.<br/>
        </span></div>
</ix:continuation>
      <ix:continuation id="Text_8897f296866c4b8b977c24fde419265928" continuedAt="Text_8897f296866c4b8b977c24fde419265929">
<div style="color: rgb(0, 0, 0); font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;"><span style="color: rgb(0, 0, 0); font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; font-style: normal; font-variant: normal; font-weight: normal; letter-spacing: normal; text-indent: 0px; text-transform: none; word-spacing: 0px; white-space: normal; background-color: rgb(255, 255, 255); text-decoration-style: initial; text-decoration-color: initial; display: inline ! important; float: none;"> <br/>
        </span></div>
</ix:continuation>
      <ix:continuation id="Text_8897f296866c4b8b977c24fde419265929" continuedAt="Text_8897f296866c4b8b977c24fde419265930">
<div style="color: rgb(0, 0, 0); font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;"><span style="color: rgb(0, 0, 0); font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; font-style: normal; font-variant: normal; font-weight: normal; letter-spacing: normal; text-indent: 0px; text-transform: none; word-spacing: 0px; white-space: normal; background-color: rgb(255, 255, 255); text-decoration-style: initial; text-decoration-color: initial; display: inline ! important; float: none;"> <span style="font-style: italic;">Wealth management customer intangible</span> - The wealth management customer intangible was valued utilizing the income approach, which employs a present value analysis, which calculates the expected after-tax cash
          flow benefits of the net revenues generated by the acquired customers over the expected lives of the acquired customers, discounted at a long-term market-oriented after-tax rate of return on investment. The value assigned to the acquired
          customers represents the future economic benefit from acquiring the customers (net of operating expenses).<br/>
        </span></div>
</ix:continuation>
      <ix:continuation id="Text_8897f296866c4b8b977c24fde419265930" continuedAt="Text_8897f296866c4b8b977c24fde419265931">
<div style="color: rgb(0, 0, 0); font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;"><span style="color: rgb(0, 0, 0); font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; font-style: normal; font-variant: normal; font-weight: normal; letter-spacing: normal; text-indent: 0px; text-transform: none; word-spacing: 0px; white-space: normal; background-color: rgb(255, 255, 255); text-decoration-style: initial; text-decoration-color: initial; display: inline ! important; float: none;"> <br/>
        </span></div>
</ix:continuation>

      <ix:continuation id="Text_8897f296866c4b8b977c24fde419265931" continuedAt="Text_8897f296866c4b8b977c24fde419265932">
<div style="color: rgb(0, 0, 0); font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;"><span style="color: rgb(0, 0, 0); font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; font-style: normal; font-variant: normal; font-weight: normal; letter-spacing: normal; text-indent: 0px; text-transform: none; word-spacing: 0px; white-space: normal; background-color: rgb(255, 255, 255); text-decoration-style: initial; text-decoration-color: initial; display: inline ! important; float: none;"> <span style="font-style: italic;">Deposits</span> - The fair value of noninterest bearing demand deposits, interest-bearing checking, money market and savings deposit accounts were assumed to approximate the carrying value as these accounts have no
          stated maturity and are payable on demand.</span> Certificate of deposit (&#8220;CD&#8221;)<span style="color: rgb(0, 0, 0); font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; font-style: normal; font-variant: normal; font-weight: normal; letter-spacing: normal; text-indent: 0px; text-transform: none; word-spacing: 0px; white-space: normal; background-color: rgb(255, 255, 255); text-decoration-style: initial; text-decoration-color: initial; display: inline ! important; float: none;"> (time
          deposit accounts) were valued at the present value of the certificates&#8217; expected contractual payments discounted at market rates for similar <span style="color: rgb(0, 0, 0); font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; font-style: normal; font-variant-ligatures: normal; font-variant-caps: normal; font-weight: 400; letter-spacing: normal; text-indent: 0px; text-transform: none; word-spacing: 0px; white-space: normal; background-color: rgb(255, 255, 255); text-decoration-style: initial; text-decoration-color: initial; display: inline ! important; float: none;">certificates which approximates carrying value.</span><br/>
        </span></div>
</ix:continuation>
      <ix:continuation id="Text_8897f296866c4b8b977c24fde419265932" continuedAt="Text_8897f296866c4b8b977c24fde419265933">
<div><br/></div>
</ix:continuation>
      <ix:continuation id="Text_8897f296866c4b8b977c24fde419265933" continuedAt="Text_8897f296866c4b8b977c24fde419265934">
<div style="color: rgb(0, 0, 0); font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;"><span style="color: rgb(0, 0, 0); font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; font-style: normal; font-variant: normal; font-weight: normal; letter-spacing: normal; text-indent: 0px; text-transform: none; word-spacing: 0px; white-space: normal; background-color: rgb(255, 255, 255); text-decoration-style: initial; text-decoration-color: initial; display: inline ! important; float: none;"> <span style="font-style: italic;">Borrowings</span> - The estimated fair value of short-term borrowings was determined to approximate stated value. <span style="color: rgb(0, 0, 0); font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; font-style: normal; font-variant-ligatures: normal; font-variant-caps: normal; font-weight: 400; letter-spacing: normal; text-indent: 0px; text-transform: none; word-spacing: 0px; white-space: normal; background-color: rgb(255, 255, 255); text-decoration-style: initial; text-decoration-color: initial; display: inline ! important; float: none;">Long-term debt, subordinated debt and junior subordinated debt were valued using a discounted cash flow approach incorporating a discount
            rate that incorporated similar terms</span><span style="font-size: 10pt;">,</span> maturity and credit rating.<br/>
        </span></div>
</ix:continuation>
      <ix:continuation id="Text_8897f296866c4b8b977c24fde419265934" continuedAt="Text_8897f296866c4b8b977c24fde419265935">
<div><br/></div>
</ix:continuation>
      <ix:continuation id="Text_8897f296866c4b8b977c24fde419265935" continuedAt="Text_8897f296866c4b8b977c24fde419265936">
<div style="color: rgb(0, 0, 0); font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;"> <span style="color: rgb(0, 0, 0); font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; font-style: italic; font-variant: normal; font-weight: normal; letter-spacing: normal; text-indent: 0px; text-transform: none; word-spacing: 0px; white-space: normal; background-color: rgb(255, 255, 255); text-decoration-style: initial; text-decoration-color: initial; display: inline ! important; float: none;">Accounting
          for Acquired Loans - </span><span style="color: rgb(0, 0, 0); font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; font-style: normal; font-variant: normal; font-weight: normal; letter-spacing: normal; text-indent: 0px; text-transform: none; word-spacing: 0px; white-space: normal; background-color: rgb(255, 255, 255); text-decoration-style: initial; text-decoration-color: initial; display: inline ! important; float: none;">Acquired loans are classified into two categories: PCD loans
          and non-PCD loans. PCD loans are defined as a loan or group of loans that have experienced more than insignificant credit deterioration since origination. Non-PCD loans had an allowance established on acquisition date, which is recognized as an
          expense through the provision for credit losses. For PCD loans, an allowance is recognized by adding it to the fair value of the loan, which is the amortized cost. There is no provision for credit loss expense recognized on PCD loans because the
          initial allowance is established by grossing-up the amortized cost of the PCD loan. The allowance for credit losses on non-PCD loans of $<ix:nonFraction name="nbtb:FinancingReceivablePurchasedWithoutCreditDeteriorationAllowanceForCreditLossAtAcquisitionDate" id="Fact_671f581446ba4e4da8c1bd0260eee6b0" contextRef="c20250502to20250502_BusinessAcquisitionAxis_EvansBancorpIncMember" unitRef="U001" decimals="-5" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal">13.0</ix:nonFraction>
          million for Evans and $<ix:nonFraction name="nbtb:FinancingReceivablePurchasedWithoutCreditDeteriorationAllowanceForCreditLossAtAcquisitionDate" id="Fact_57c825268df24b36a9e7b66dc1ddc629" contextRef="c20230811to20230811_BusinessAcquisitionAxis_SalisburyBancorpIncMember" unitRef="U001" decimals="-5" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal">8.8</ix:nonFraction> million for Salisbury was recorded through the provision for loan losses within the consolidated statements
          of income.</span><span style="font-weight: normal; color: rgb(0, 0, 0); font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; font-style: normal; font-variant: normal; text-transform: none;"> <ix:nonNumeric name="nbtb:FairValueOfAcquiredPCDLoans" id="Text_510e5929cd824f10ba72e859be59dd46" contextRef="c20250101to20251231" escape="true" continuedAt="Text_4ef88fec6ddd47968c90dfee78b4adc11"><span style="color: rgb(0, 0, 0); font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; font-style: normal; font-variant: normal; font-weight: normal;">The following table provides details related to the fair value of acquired PCD loans.
        </span></ix:nonNumeric></span> </div>
</ix:continuation>

      respectively, represented a credit loss impairment. AFS debt securities in unrealized loss positions are evaluated for impairment related to credit losses at least quarterly. As of December 31, 2025 and 2024, the majority of the AFS securities in an
      unrealized loss position consisted of debt securities issued by U.S. government agencies or U.S. government-sponsored enterprises that carry the explicit and/or implicit guarantee of the U.S. government, which are widely recognized as &#8220;risk-free&#8221; and
      have a long history of zero credit losses. Total gross unrealized losses were primarily attributable to changes in interest rates, relative to when the investment securities were purchased, and not due to the credit quality of the investment
      securities. The Company does not intend to sell, nor is it more likely than not that the Company will be required to sell the securities before recovery of their amortized cost basis, which may be at maturity. The Company elected to exclude AIR from
      the amortized cost basis of debt securities.       not rated. Based on the Company&#8217;s CECL methodology, the expected credit loss on the HTM municipal bond portfolio was deemed immaterial, therefore no allowance for credit loss was recorded as of December 31, 2025 and 2024. AIR on HTM debt securities
      totaled $<ix:nonFraction name="us-gaap:DebtSecuritiesHeldToMaturityAccruedInterestAfterAllowanceForCreditLoss" id="Fact_37955db7b4e847f4a2afe41cd680fe27" contextRef="c20251231" unitRef="U001" decimals="-5" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal">3.9</ix:nonFraction> million and $<ix:nonFraction name="us-gaap:DebtSecuritiesHeldToMaturityAccruedInterestAfterAllowanceForCreditLoss" id="Fact_85276f0cd50b40c8a4635d80695aed60" contextRef="c20241231" unitRef="U001" decimals="-5" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal">4.4</ix:nonFraction>

      <ix:nonNumeric name="nbtb:FinancingReceivableHeldForInvestmentAllowanceAndNonperformingLoansPolicyTextBlock" id="Text_ba7b714e1a564980aa5f779d68eac632" contextRef="c20250101to20251231" escape="true" continuedAt="Text_e921c6b28a4e406ebea87b42235826dd1"><ix:continuation id="Text_f861f05f3eff490bbd1b51d45c8119f34" continuedAt="Text_f861f05f3eff490bbd1b51d45c8119f35">
<div style="text-align: justify; color: #000000; font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">The allowance for credit losses calculation incorporated a 6-quarter forecast period to account for forecast economic conditions under each scenario
        utilized in the measurement. For periods beyond the 6-quarter forecast, the model reverts to long-term economic conditions over a 4-quarter reversion period on a straight-line basis. The Company considers a baseline, upside and downside economic
        forecast in measuring the allowance. Starting in the second quarter of 2025, the Company included an additional downside scenario with stagflation conditions, which is characterized as an economic environment where inflation rises alongside
        unemployment. Stagflation was identified as an emerging risk as tariff policies impacted the economy.<br/>
      </div>
</ix:continuation></ix:nonNumeric>
      <ix:continuation id="Text_e921c6b28a4e406ebea87b42235826dd1" continuedAt="Text_e921c6b28a4e406ebea87b42235826dd2"><ix:continuation id="Text_f861f05f3eff490bbd1b51d45c8119f35" continuedAt="Text_f861f05f3eff490bbd1b51d45c8119f36">
<div style="text-align: justify; color: #000000; font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;"> <br/>
      </div>
</ix:continuation></ix:continuation>
      <ix:continuation id="Text_e921c6b28a4e406ebea87b42235826dd2" continuedAt="Text_e921c6b28a4e406ebea87b42235826dd3"><ix:continuation id="Text_f861f05f3eff490bbd1b51d45c8119f36" continuedAt="Text_f861f05f3eff490bbd1b51d45c8119f37">
<div style="text-align: justify; color: #000000; font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">The quantitative model as of December 31, 2025 incorporated a baseline economic outlook along with an alternative upside scenario and two equally
        weighted downside scenarios, recessionary conditions and stagflation, sourced from a reputable third-party to accommodate other potential economic conditions in the model. At December 31, 2025, the weightings were 65%, 5% and 30% for the baseline,
        upside and downside economic forecast scenarios, respectively. The baseline outlook reflected an economic environment where the northeast unemployment rate increases from 4.5% in the first quarter of 2026 to 4.8% by the end of the forecast period,
        with a peak northeast unemployment rate of 4.9% in the fourth quarter of 2026. National Gross Domestic Product (&#8220;GDP&#8221;) annualized growth (on a quarterly basis) is expected to start the first quarter of 2026 at approximately 2.55% and decrease to
        1.8% by the end of the forecast period. Key assumptions in the baseline economic outlook included the Federal Reserve cutting rates with one 25 basis point cut at the December meeting and the economy remaining at full employment. The alternative
        upside scenario assumes improved economic conditions from the baseline outlook. Under this scenario, northeast unemployment falls from 4.4% in the fourth quarter of 2025 to 4.0% in the second quarter of 2026 and eventually settles at 4.1% by the
        end of the forecast period. The alternative downside scenario with recessionary conditions assumes deteriorated economic conditions from the baseline outlook. Under this scenario, northeast unemployment rises from 4.4% in the fourth quarter of 2025
        to a peak of 7.8% in the first quarter of 2027. The alternative downside stagflation scenario assumes deteriorated economic conditions from the baseline outlook. Under this scenario, northeast unemployment rises from 4.4% in the fourth quarter of
        2025 to 6% by the end of the forecast period in the second quarter of 2027, with a peak northeast unemployment rate of 8.2% in the first quarter of 2028. These scenarios and their respective weightings are evaluated at each measurement date and
        reflect management&#8217;s expectations as of December 31, 2025. Additional qualitative adjustments were made for factors not incorporated in the forecasts or the model, such as loss rate expectations for certain loan pools, reversion adjustments for the
        stagflation scenario and recent trends in asset value indices. Additional monitoring for industry concentrations, loan growth and policy exceptions was also conducted.<br/>
      </div>
</ix:continuation></ix:continuation>
      <ix:continuation id="Text_e921c6b28a4e406ebea87b42235826dd3" continuedAt="Text_e921c6b28a4e406ebea87b42235826dd4"><ix:continuation id="Text_f861f05f3eff490bbd1b51d45c8119f37" continuedAt="Text_f861f05f3eff490bbd1b51d45c8119f38">
<div style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;"><br/>

<div style="text-align: justify; color: #000000; font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">The quantitative model as of December 31, 2024 incorporated a baseline economic outlook along with an alternative downside scenario sourced from a
        reputable third-party to accommodate other potential economic conditions in the model. At December 31, 2024, the weightings were 80% and 20% for the baseline and downside economic forecasts, respectively. The baseline outlook reflected a northeast
        unemployment rate environment starting at 4.1% and increasing slightly during the forecast period to 4.2%. Northeast GDP annualized growth (on a quarterly basis) is expected to start the first quarter of 2025 at approximately 3.8% before decreasing
        to a low of 2.6% in the third quarter of 2025 and then increasing to 3.9% by the end of the forecast period. Key assumptions in the baseline economic outlook included <span style="background-color: rgb(255, 255, 255); font-weight: normal; color: rgb(0, 0, 0); font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; font-style: normal; font-variant: normal; text-transform: none;">two 25 basis point federal funds rate cuts in 2025, quantitative tightening ending in early 2025, a post-election
          fiscal outlook with lower spending, lower taxes, and higher tariffs, and the economy currently being near full employment.</span> The alternative downside scenario assumed deteriorated economic conditions from the baseline outlook. Under this
        scenario, northeast unemployment increases to a peak of 7.5% in the first quarter of 2026. These scenarios and their respective weightings are evaluated at each measurement date and reflect management&#8217;s expectations as of December 31, 2024.
        Additional qualitative adjustments were made for factors not incorporated in the forecasts or the model, such as loss rate expectations for certain loan pools, considerations for inflation and recent trends in asset value indices. Additional
        monitoring for industry concentrations, loan growth and policy exceptions was also conducted. </div>
</ix:continuation></ix:continuation>

          Under this scenario, northeast unemployment increases to a peak of 7.0% in the first quarter of 2025. These scenarios and their respective weightings are evaluated at each measurement date and reflect management&#8217;s expectations as of December 31,
          2023. Additional qualitative adjustments were made for factors not incorporated in the forecasts or the model, such as loss rate expectations for certain loan pools, considerations for inflation and recent trends in asset value indices.
          Additional monitoring for industry concentrations, loan growth and policy exceptions was also conducted.</span></div>

<div style="text-align: justify; font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; font-weight: bold;">Credit Quality Indicators</div>
</ix:continuation>
      <ix:continuation id="Text_f861f05f3eff490bbd1b51d45c8119f336" continuedAt="Text_f861f05f3eff490bbd1b51d45c8119f337">
<div><span style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;"><br/>
        </span> </div>
</ix:continuation>
      <ix:continuation id="Text_f861f05f3eff490bbd1b51d45c8119f337" continuedAt="Text_f861f05f3eff490bbd1b51d45c8119f338">
<div style="text-align: justify; font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">The Company has developed an internal loan grading system to evaluate and quantify the Company&#8217;s loan portfolio with respect to quality and risk, focusing on, among
        other things, borrower&#8217;s financial strength, experience and depth of borrower&#8217;s management, primary and secondary sources of repayment, payment history, nature of the business and industry outlook. The internal grading system enables the Company to
        monitor the quality of the entire loan portfolio on a consistent basis and provide management with an early warning system, which facilitates recognition of and response to problem loans and potential problem loans.</div>
</ix:continuation>

          <div><a href="#TABLEOFCONTENTS"><span style="font-size: 8pt; font-style: italic;">Table of Contents</span></a></div>

      <ix:continuation id="Text_f861f05f3eff490bbd1b51d45c8119f339" continuedAt="Text_f861f05f3eff490bbd1b51d45c8119f340">
<div style="text-align: justify; font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; font-weight: bold;">Commercial Grading System</div>
</ix:continuation>
      <ix:continuation id="Text_f861f05f3eff490bbd1b51d45c8119f340" continuedAt="Text_f861f05f3eff490bbd1b51d45c8119f341">
<div><span style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;"><br/>
        </span> </div>
</ix:continuation>
      <ix:continuation id="Text_f861f05f3eff490bbd1b51d45c8119f341" continuedAt="Text_f861f05f3eff490bbd1b51d45c8119f342">
<div style="text-align: justify; font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">For C&amp;I and CRE loans, the Company uses a grading system that relies on quantifiable and measurable characteristics when available. This includes comparison of
        financial strength to available industry averages, comparison of transaction factors (loan terms and conditions) to loan policy and comparison of credit history to stated repayment terms and industry averages. Some grading factors are necessarily
        more subjective such as economic and industry factors, regulatory environment and management. C&amp;I and CRE loans are graded Doubtful, Substandard, Special Mention and Pass.</div>
</ix:continuation>
      <ix:continuation id="Text_f861f05f3eff490bbd1b51d45c8119f342" continuedAt="Text_f861f05f3eff490bbd1b51d45c8119f343">
<div><span style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;"><br/>
        </span> </div>
</ix:continuation>
      <ix:continuation id="Text_f861f05f3eff490bbd1b51d45c8119f343" continuedAt="Text_f861f05f3eff490bbd1b51d45c8119f344">
<div style="text-align: justify; font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;"><span style="font-style: italic;">Doubtful </span>- A Doubtful loan has a high probability of total or substantial loss, but because of specific pending events that
        may strengthen the asset, its classification as a loss is deferred. Doubtful borrowers are usually in default, lack adequate liquidity or capital and lack the resources necessary to remain an operating entity. Pending events can include mergers,
        acquisitions, liquidations, capital injections, the perfection of liens on additional collateral, the valuation of collateral and refinancing. Generally, pending events should be resolved within a relatively short period and the ratings will be
        adjusted based on the new information. Nonaccrual treatment is required for Doubtful assets because of the high probability of loss.</div>
</ix:continuation>
      <ix:continuation id="Text_f861f05f3eff490bbd1b51d45c8119f344" continuedAt="Text_f861f05f3eff490bbd1b51d45c8119f345">
<div style="text-align: justify; margin-left: 18pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;"> <br/>
      </div>
</ix:continuation>
      <ix:continuation id="Text_f861f05f3eff490bbd1b51d45c8119f345" continuedAt="Text_f861f05f3eff490bbd1b51d45c8119f346">
<div><span style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;"> </span></div>
</ix:continuation>
      <div style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; text-align: justify;">
        <ix:continuation id="Text_f861f05f3eff490bbd1b51d45c8119f346" continuedAt="Text_f861f05f3eff490bbd1b51d45c8119f347">
<div style="text-align: justify; font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;"><span style="font-style: italic;">Substandard </span>- Substandard loans have a high probability of payment default or they have other well-defined weaknesses. They
          require more intensive supervision by bank management. Substandard loans are generally characterized by current or expected unprofitable operations, inadequate debt service coverage, inadequate liquidity or marginal capitalization. Repayment may
          depend on collateral or other credit risk mitigants. For some Substandard loans, the likelihood of full collection of interest and principal may be in doubt and those loans should be placed on nonaccrual. Although Substandard assets in the
          aggregate will have a distinct potential for loss, an individual asset&#8217;s loss potential does not have to be distinct for the asset to be rated Substandard.</div>
</ix:continuation>
      </div>

      <ix:continuation id="Text_f861f05f3eff490bbd1b51d45c8119f347" continuedAt="Text_f861f05f3eff490bbd1b51d45c8119f348">
<div style="text-align: justify;"><span style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;"><br/>
        </span> </div>
</ix:continuation>
      <!--PROfilePageNumberReset%Num%79%%%-->
      <ix:continuation id="Text_f861f05f3eff490bbd1b51d45c8119f348" continuedAt="Text_f861f05f3eff490bbd1b51d45c8119f349">
<div style="text-align: justify; font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;"><span style="font-style: italic;">Special Mention</span> - Special Mention loans have potential weaknesses that may, if not checked or corrected, weaken the asset or
        inadequately protect the Company&#8217;s position at some future date. These loans pose elevated risk, but their weakness does not yet justify a Substandard classification. Borrowers may be experiencing adverse operating trends (i.e., declining revenues
        or margins) or may be struggling with an ill-proportioned balance sheet (i.e., increasing inventory without an increase in sales, high leverage and/or tight liquidity). Adverse economic or market conditions, such as interest rate increases or the
        entry of a new competitor, may also support a Special Mention rating. Although a Special Mention loan has a higher PD than a Pass asset, its default is not imminent.</div>
</ix:continuation>
      <ix:continuation id="Text_f861f05f3eff490bbd1b51d45c8119f349" continuedAt="Text_f861f05f3eff490bbd1b51d45c8119f350">
<div><br/>
      </div>
</ix:continuation>
      <ix:continuation id="Text_f861f05f3eff490bbd1b51d45c8119f350" continuedAt="Text_f861f05f3eff490bbd1b51d45c8119f351">
<div style="text-align: justify; font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;"><span style="font-style: italic;">Pass</span> - Loans graded as Pass encompass all loans not graded as Doubtful, Substandard or Special Mention.&#160;Pass loans are in
        compliance with loan covenants and payments are generally made as agreed.&#160;Pass loans range from superior quality to fair quality. Pass loans also include any portion of a government guaranteed loan, including Paycheck Protection Program loans.</div>
</ix:continuation>
      <ix:continuation id="Text_f861f05f3eff490bbd1b51d45c8119f351" continuedAt="Text_f861f05f3eff490bbd1b51d45c8119f352">
<div><br/></div>
</ix:continuation>
      <ix:continuation id="Text_f861f05f3eff490bbd1b51d45c8119f352" continuedAt="Text_f861f05f3eff490bbd1b51d45c8119f353">
<div style="text-align: justify; color: rgb(0, 0, 0); font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; font-weight: bold;">Consumer and Residential Grading System</div>
</ix:continuation>
      <ix:continuation id="Text_f861f05f3eff490bbd1b51d45c8119f353" continuedAt="Text_f861f05f3eff490bbd1b51d45c8119f354">
<div><span style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;"><br/>
        </span> </div>
</ix:continuation>
      <ix:continuation id="Text_f861f05f3eff490bbd1b51d45c8119f354" continuedAt="Text_f861f05f3eff490bbd1b51d45c8119f355">
<div style="text-align: justify; color: rgb(0, 0, 0); font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">Consumer and Residential loans are graded as either Nonperforming or Performing.</div>
</ix:continuation>
      <ix:continuation id="Text_f861f05f3eff490bbd1b51d45c8119f355" continuedAt="Text_f861f05f3eff490bbd1b51d45c8119f356">
<div style="text-align: justify; margin-left: 18pt; color: rgb(0, 0, 0); font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; font-weight: bold;"> <br/>
      </div>
</ix:continuation>
      <ix:continuation id="Text_f861f05f3eff490bbd1b51d45c8119f356" continuedAt="Text_f861f05f3eff490bbd1b51d45c8119f357">
<div style="text-align: justify; color: rgb(0, 0, 0); font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;"><span style="font-style: italic;">Nonperforming </span>- Nonperforming loans are loans that are (1) over <ix:nonNumeric name="nbtb:ThresholdPeriodPastDueForLoansToBeConsideredNonperforming" id="Fact_6bd8e408b792483682daaa2260e0e171" contextRef="c20250101to20251231" format="ixt-sec:durday">90</ix:nonNumeric> days past due and interest is still accruing or (2) on nonaccrual status.</div>
</ix:continuation>
      <ix:continuation id="Text_f861f05f3eff490bbd1b51d45c8119f357" continuedAt="Text_f861f05f3eff490bbd1b51d45c8119f358">
<div><span style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;"><br/>
        </span> </div>
</ix:continuation>
      <ix:continuation id="Text_f861f05f3eff490bbd1b51d45c8119f358" continuedAt="Text_f861f05f3eff490bbd1b51d45c8119f359">
<div style="text-align: justify; color: rgb(0, 0, 0); font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; font-weight: bold;"><span style="font-weight: normal; font-style: italic;">Performing </span>- <span style="font-weight: normal;">All loans not
          meeting any of the above criteria are considered Performing.</span></div>
</ix:continuation>
      <ix:continuation id="Text_f861f05f3eff490bbd1b51d45c8119f359" continuedAt="Text_f861f05f3eff490bbd1b51d45c8119f360">
<div style="text-align: justify; color: rgb(0, 0, 0); font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;"><span style="font-size: 10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman'; color: rgb(0, 0, 0);"> <br/>
        </span></div>
</ix:continuation>
    </div>

      <div style="text-align: justify; font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;"><ix:nonNumeric name="nbtb:LoanModificationsToBorrowersExperiencingFinancialDifficultiesPolicyTextBlock" id="Text_1e8de88aab8e42d4a18051dd3e6392f7" contextRef="c20250101to20251231" escape="true" continuedAt="Text_4378151597804e83ad436b2f379909401"><ix:continuation id="Text_f861f05f3eff490bbd1b51d45c8119f370" continuedAt="Text_f861f05f3eff490bbd1b51d45c8119f371">
<div><span style="font-size: 10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-weight: bold;">Loan Modifications to Borrowers Experiencing Financial Difficulties</span><br/></div>
</ix:continuation></ix:nonNumeric>
        <ix:continuation id="Text_4378151597804e83ad436b2f379909401"><ix:continuation id="Text_f861f05f3eff490bbd1b51d45c8119f371" continuedAt="Text_f861f05f3eff490bbd1b51d45c8119f372">
<div style="text-align: justify; color: rgb(0, 0, 0); font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;"><span style="font-size: 10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman';"><br/>
          </span>The Company&#8217;s January 1, 2023 adoption of ASU 2022-02 eliminates the recognition and measurement of TDRs. Upon adoption of this guidance, the Company no longer recognizes an allowance for credit losses for the economic concession granted
          to a borrower for changes in the timing and amount of contractual cash flows when a loan is restructured. The adoption of ASU 2022-02 resulted in a change to reporting for loan modifications to borrowers experiencing financial difficulties. With
          the adoption of ASU 2022-02 these modifications required enhanced reporting on the type of modifications granted and the financial magnitude of the concessions granted.<br/>
          <span style="font-size: 10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman';"><br/>
          </span>When the Company modifies a loan with financial difficulty, such modifications generally include one or a combination of the following: an extension of the maturity date; a stated rate of interest lower than the current market rate for new
          debt with similar risk; a change in scheduled payment amount; or principal forgiveness.</div>
</ix:continuation></ix:continuation>
      </div>

    <ix:nonNumeric name="nbtb:PropertyPlantAndEquipmentEstimatedUsefulLivesPolicyTextBlock" id="Text_5007693df0e349d9a6b050f4dd2d4d9e" contextRef="c20250101to20251231" escape="true"><ix:continuation id="Text_03f1e6c08c9145b6a6dd09ecb336712d7" continuedAt="Text_03f1e6c08c9145b6a6dd09ecb336712d8">
<div style="text-align: justify; font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">Buildings and improvements are depreciated based on useful lives of <span style="-sec-ix-hidden:Fact_fba4afe298574d89a975a9ec346952d9">five</span>
      to <ix:nonNumeric name="us-gaap:PropertyPlantAndEquipmentUsefulLife" id="Fact_e517a914c9d14c48a0537779035f5430" contextRef="c20251231_PropertyPlantAndEquipmentByTypeAxis_BuildingAndBuildingImprovementsMember_RangeAxis_MaximumMember" format="ixt-sec:durwordsen">twenty years</ix:nonNumeric>. Furniture and equipment is depreciated based on useful lives of <span style="-sec-ix-hidden:Fact_afc36dbb24a043c89c08abc1449995e8">three</span> to <ix:nonNumeric name="us-gaap:PropertyPlantAndEquipmentUsefulLife" id="Fact_4fab3f3b6940428bbd8d97d50d6338f9" contextRef="c20251231_PropertyPlantAndEquipmentByTypeAxis_EquipmentMember_RangeAxis_MaximumMember" format="ixt-sec:durwordsen">ten years</ix:nonNumeric>.</div>
</ix:continuation></ix:nonNumeric>

    <ix:continuation id="Text_03f1e6c08c9145b6a6dd09ecb336712d8" continuedAt="Text_03f1e6c08c9145b6a6dd09ecb336712d9">
<div><br/>
    </div>
</ix:continuation>

    <ix:nonNumeric name="nbtb:LesseeOperatingLeasesPolicyTextBlock" id="Text_ff16d3f1e106419ebb4354cb58dd6a8e" contextRef="c20250101to20251231" escape="true" continuedAt="Text_89f8e48704ec4ef2858a1dce9e77f2e41"><ix:continuation id="Text_03f1e6c08c9145b6a6dd09ecb336712d9" continuedAt="Text_03f1e6c08c9145b6a6dd09ecb336712d10">
<div style="text-align: justify; color: rgb(0, 0, 0); font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">Operating leases in which the Company is the lessee are recorded as operating lease ROU assets and operating lease liabilities, included in <span style="-sec-ix-hidden:Fact_414d2e06950d47839d55a567e3ebe861"><span style="-sec-ix-hidden:Fact_14c6b51643c84722b4611680e51f965a">other assets</span></span> and <span style="-sec-ix-hidden:Fact_3f36e982753d402d9b900b6a765fc1db"><span style="-sec-ix-hidden:Fact_28da96d6854147caa6e4722f294f173b">other liabilities</span></span>,
      respectively, on the consolidated balance sheets. The Company does not have any significant finance leases in which we are the lessee as of December 31, 2025 and December 31, 2024.</div>
</ix:continuation></ix:nonNumeric>
    <ix:continuation id="Text_89f8e48704ec4ef2858a1dce9e77f2e41" continuedAt="Text_89f8e48704ec4ef2858a1dce9e77f2e42"><ix:continuation id="Text_03f1e6c08c9145b6a6dd09ecb336712d10" continuedAt="Text_03f1e6c08c9145b6a6dd09ecb336712d11">
<div><br/>
    </div>
</ix:continuation></ix:continuation>
    <ix:continuation id="Text_89f8e48704ec4ef2858a1dce9e77f2e42" continuedAt="Text_89f8e48704ec4ef2858a1dce9e77f2e43"><ix:continuation id="Text_03f1e6c08c9145b6a6dd09ecb336712d11" continuedAt="Text_03f1e6c08c9145b6a6dd09ecb336712d12">
<div style="text-align: justify; color: rgb(0, 0, 0); font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">Operating lease ROU assets represent the Company&#8217;s right to use an underlying asset during the lease term and operating lease liabilities represent
      our obligation to make lease payments arising from the lease. ROU assets and operating lease liabilities are recognized at lease commencement based on the present value of the remaining lease payments using a discount rate that represents the
      Company&#8217;s incremental borrowing rate at the lease commencement date. ROU assets are further adjusted for lease incentives. Operating lease expense, which is comprised of amortization of the ROU asset and the implicit interest accreted on the
      operating lease liability, is recognized on a straight-line basis over the lease term and is recorded in occupancy expense in the consolidated statements of income.</div>
</ix:continuation></ix:continuation>
    <ix:continuation id="Text_89f8e48704ec4ef2858a1dce9e77f2e43" continuedAt="Text_89f8e48704ec4ef2858a1dce9e77f2e44"><ix:continuation id="Text_03f1e6c08c9145b6a6dd09ecb336712d12" continuedAt="Text_03f1e6c08c9145b6a6dd09ecb336712d13">
<div><br/></div>
</ix:continuation></ix:continuation>
    <ix:continuation id="Text_89f8e48704ec4ef2858a1dce9e77f2e44" continuedAt="Text_89f8e48704ec4ef2858a1dce9e77f2e45"><ix:continuation id="Text_03f1e6c08c9145b6a6dd09ecb336712d13" continuedAt="Text_03f1e6c08c9145b6a6dd09ecb336712d14">
<div style="text-align: justify; color: rgb(0, 0, 0); font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">The Company made a policy election to exclude the recognition requirements to all classes of leases with original terms of 12 months or less.
      Instead, the short-term lease payments are recognized in profit or loss on a straight-line basis over the lease term.</div>
</ix:continuation></ix:continuation>
    <ix:continuation id="Text_89f8e48704ec4ef2858a1dce9e77f2e45" continuedAt="Text_89f8e48704ec4ef2858a1dce9e77f2e46"><ix:continuation id="Text_03f1e6c08c9145b6a6dd09ecb336712d14" continuedAt="Text_03f1e6c08c9145b6a6dd09ecb336712d15">
<div><br/>
    </div>

    <ix:continuation id="Text_89f8e48704ec4ef2858a1dce9e77f2e46" continuedAt="Text_89f8e48704ec4ef2858a1dce9e77f2e47"><ix:continuation id="Text_03f1e6c08c9145b6a6dd09ecb336712d15" continuedAt="Text_03f1e6c08c9145b6a6dd09ecb336712d16">
<div style="text-align: justify; color: rgb(0, 0, 0); font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">The Company has lease agreements with lease and non-lease components, which are generally accounted for separately. For real estate leases,
      non-lease components and other non-components, such as common area maintenance charges, real estate taxes and insurance are not included in the measurement of the lease liability since they are generally able to be segregated.</div>
</ix:continuation></ix:continuation>

<div><br/>

<div style="text-align: justify; color: rgb(0, 0, 0); font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">Our leases relate primarily to office space and bank branches, and some contain options to renew the lease. These options to renew are generally not
      considered reasonably certain to exercise, and are therefore not included in the lease term until such time that the option to renew is reasonably certain. As of December 31, 2025, operating lease ROU assets and liabilities were $<ix:nonFraction name="us-gaap:OperatingLeaseRightOfUseAsset" id="Fact_700ad96439c54bacab044a65699182dd" contextRef="c20251231" unitRef="U001" decimals="-5" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal">30.6</ix:nonFraction> million and <span style="background-color: rgb(255, 255, 255); font-weight: normal; color: rgb(0, 0, 0); font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; font-style: normal; font-variant: normal; text-transform: none;">$<ix:nonFraction name="us-gaap:OperatingLeaseLiability" id="Fact_608b960fb9e64cab941a6d5afb1a8a6e" contextRef="c20251231" unitRef="U001" decimals="-5" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal">33.1</ix:nonFraction> million, respectively</span>. As of December 31, 2024,
      operating lease ROU assets and liabilities were $<ix:nonFraction name="us-gaap:OperatingLeaseRightOfUseAsset" id="Fact_460e6c8c85734249a2708dad40a2f1ce" contextRef="c20241231" unitRef="U001" decimals="-5" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal">27.6</ix:nonFraction> million and $<ix:nonFraction name="us-gaap:OperatingLeaseLiability" id="Fact_b0f25ce1935e4f43b4f8b50dfd709895" contextRef="c20241231" unitRef="U001" decimals="-5" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal">30.3</ix:nonFraction> million, respectively.</div>

<div style="text-align: justify; color: rgb(0, 0, 0); font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">The Company&#8217;s junior subordinated debentures are redeemable prior to the maturity date at our option upon each trust&#8217;s stated option repurchase
          dates and from time to time thereafter. These debentures are also redeemable in whole at any time upon the occurrence of specific events defined within the trust indenture. Our obligations under the debentures and related documents, taken
          together, constitute a full and unconditional guarantee by the Company of the issuers&#8217; obligations under the trust preferred securities. The Company owns all of the common stock of the Trusts, which have issued trust preferred securities in
          conjunction with the Company issuing trust preferred debentures to the Trusts. The terms of the trust preferred debentures are substantially the same as the terms of the trust preferred securities.</div>
</ix:continuation>

<div style="text-align: justify; color: rgb(0, 0, 0); font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">With respect to the Trusts, the Company has the right to defer payments of interest on the debentures issued to the Trusts at any time or from
          time to time for a period of up to <ix:nonFraction name="nbtb:DistributionDeferralPeriodSubordinatedDebentures" id="Fact_433c698891cc49e4991ea5ae0e13462a" contextRef="c20250101to20251231_LegalEntityAxis_CombinedTrustsMember" unitRef="U012" decimals="INF" scale="0" format="ixt-sec:numwordsen">ten</ix:nonFraction> consecutive semi-annual periods with respect to each deferral period. Under the terms of the
          debentures, if in certain circumstances there is an event of default under the debentures or the Company elects to defer interest on the debentures, the Company may not, with certain exceptions, declare or pay any dividends or distributions on
          its capital stock or purchase or acquire any of its capital stock.</div>

<div style="text-align: justify; color: rgb(0, 0, 0); font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">Despite the fact that the Trusts are not included in the Company&#8217;s consolidated financial statements, $<ix:nonFraction name="nbtb:TrustPreferredSecuritiesIncludedTierOneCapital" id="Fact_30cc840e70df45e4a164aab1e0c79d11" contextRef="c20251231_LegalEntityAxis_CombinedTrustsMember" unitRef="U001" decimals="-6" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal">108</ix:nonFraction> million of the $<ix:nonFraction name="nbtb:DebtInstrumentAmountOwedToTrust" id="Fact_21b3ca353b6646368eb71a50b75d19b8" contextRef="c20251231_LegalEntityAxis_CombinedTrustsMember" unitRef="U001" decimals="-6" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal">112</ix:nonFraction> million in trust preferred securities
          issued by these subsidiary trusts was included in the Tier 1 capital of the Company for regulatory capital purposes as allowed by the FRB (NBT Bank owns $<ix:nonFraction name="us-gaap:EquityMethodInvestments" id="Fact_cfd466780c3b434d969cc07ca5d10917" contextRef="c20251231_ConsolidatedEntitiesAxis_ParentCompanyMember" unitRef="U001" decimals="-5" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal">1.0</ix:nonFraction>
          million of CNBF Trust I securities) through March 31, 2025. The Dodd-Frank Wall Street Reform and Consumer Protection Act of 2010 requires bank holding companies with assets greater than $<ix:nonFraction name="nbtb:MinimumAssetsForBankHoldingCompaniesToBeSubjectToSameCapitalRequirementsAsInsuredDepositoryInstitutions" id="Fact_b011ae34715640e59e33b14b407a4e0e" contextRef="c20251231" unitRef="U001" decimals="-6" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal">500</ix:nonFraction> million to be subject to the same capital requirements as insured depository institutions, meaning, for instance, that such bank holding companies will not be able to
          count trust preferred securities issued after May 19, 2010 as Tier 1 capital. The aforementioned Trusts are grandfathered with respect to this enactment based on their date of issuance.&#160; As of June 30, 2025 in connection with the completion of
          the Evans acquisition and the Company&#8217;s assets exceeding $15 billion, the Trusts are now included in the Company&#8217;s Tier 2 capital for regulatory capital purposes. <br/>

<div style="text-align: justify; font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">Realization of deferred tax assets is dependent upon the generation of future taxable income.&#160;A valuation allowance is recorded when it is more likely than not that
        some portion of the deferred tax asset will not be realized.&#160;Based on available evidence, gross deferred tax assets will ultimately be realized and a valuation allowance was not deemed necessary at December 31, 2025 and 2024.</div>

<div style="text-align: justify; font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;"><span style="font-size: 10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-weight: bold;">12.</span>&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;<span style="font-size: 10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-weight: bold;">Employee Benefit Plans</span></div>
</ix:nonNumeric>
    <div style="text-align: justify; font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">
      <ix:continuation id="Text_011b9813f17f41a5b27a5e52aa0fa32d1" continuedAt="Text_011b9813f17f41a5b27a5e52aa0fa32d2"><hr style="height: 2px; color: #000000; background-color: #000000; text-align: center; border: none; margin-left: auto; margin-right: auto;"/></ix:continuation></div>

    <ix:nonNumeric name="us-gaap:PostemploymentBenefitPlansPolicy" id="Text_7a0fd46d70204677ab866893cb9f3e7f" contextRef="c20250101to20251231" escape="true" continuedAt="Text_3352c7f9313745d9830a22d42ede9cba1"><ix:continuation id="Text_011b9813f17f41a5b27a5e52aa0fa32d3" continuedAt="Text_011b9813f17f41a5b27a5e52aa0fa32d4">
<div style="text-align: left; font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; font-weight: bold;">Defined Benefit Post-Retirement Plans</div>
</ix:continuation></ix:nonNumeric>
    <ix:continuation id="Text_3352c7f9313745d9830a22d42ede9cba1" continuedAt="Text_3352c7f9313745d9830a22d42ede9cba2"><ix:continuation id="Text_011b9813f17f41a5b27a5e52aa0fa32d4" continuedAt="Text_011b9813f17f41a5b27a5e52aa0fa32d5">
<div><br/>
    </div>
</ix:continuation></ix:continuation>
    <ix:continuation id="Text_3352c7f9313745d9830a22d42ede9cba2" continuedAt="Text_3352c7f9313745d9830a22d42ede9cba3"><ix:continuation id="Text_011b9813f17f41a5b27a5e52aa0fa32d5" continuedAt="Text_011b9813f17f41a5b27a5e52aa0fa32d6">
<div style="text-align: justify; font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">The Company has a qualified, noncontributory, defined benefit pension plan (the &#8220;Plan&#8221;) covering substantially all of its employees at December 31, 2025. Benefits paid
      from the Plan are based on age, years of service, compensation and social security benefits and are determined in accordance with defined formulas. The Company&#8217;s policy is to fund the Plan in accordance with Employee Retirement Income Security Act of
      1974 standards. Assets of the Plan are invested in publicly traded stocks, bonds and mutual funds. Prior to January 1, 2000, the Plan was a traditional defined benefit plan based on final average compensation. On January 1, 2000, the Plan was
      converted to a cash balance plan with grandfathering provisions for existing participants. Effective March 1, 2013, the Plan was amended. Benefit accruals for participants who, as of January 1, 2000, elected to continue participating in the
      traditional defined benefit plan design were frozen as of March 1, 2013. In addition to the Plan, the Company provides supplemental employee retirement plans to certain current and former executives. These supplemental employee retirement plans and
      the Plan are collectively referred to herein as &#8220;Pension Benefits.&#8221;</div>
</ix:continuation></ix:continuation>
    <ix:continuation id="Text_3352c7f9313745d9830a22d42ede9cba3" continuedAt="Text_3352c7f9313745d9830a22d42ede9cba4"><ix:continuation id="Text_011b9813f17f41a5b27a5e52aa0fa32d6" continuedAt="Text_011b9813f17f41a5b27a5e52aa0fa32d7">
<div style="text-align: justify; font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;"> <br/>
    </div>
</ix:continuation></ix:continuation>
    <ix:continuation id="Text_3352c7f9313745d9830a22d42ede9cba4" continuedAt="Text_3352c7f9313745d9830a22d42ede9cba5"><ix:continuation id="Text_011b9813f17f41a5b27a5e52aa0fa32d7" continuedAt="Text_011b9813f17f41a5b27a5e52aa0fa32d8">
<div style="text-align: justify; font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;"><span style="background-color: rgb(255, 255, 255); font-weight: normal; color: rgb(0, 0, 0); font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; font-style: normal; font-variant: normal; text-transform: none;"> In connection with the Evans acquisition, the Company assumed the non-contributory, qualified, defined benefit pension plan and the nonqualified supplemental executive retirement plans. Effective May 2,
        2025, the Evans defined benefit pension plan was merged into the Plan. The merging of the plans required a valuation as of the merger date and resulted in a $<ix:nonFraction name="nbtb:DefinedBenefitPlanEffectOfPlanAmendmentsAndOtherEventsRecognizedInOtherComprehensiveIncome" id="Fact_340000e81b934146846dc0cd7753a656" contextRef="c20250502to20250502" unitRef="U001" decimals="-5" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal">0.9</ix:nonFraction> million adjustment to AOCI. The merging of the plans did not have a significant impact on the Company&#8217;s financial statements and related footnotes.</span><br/>
    </div>
</ix:continuation></ix:continuation>
    <ix:continuation id="Text_3352c7f9313745d9830a22d42ede9cba5" continuedAt="Text_3352c7f9313745d9830a22d42ede9cba6"><ix:continuation id="Text_011b9813f17f41a5b27a5e52aa0fa32d8" continuedAt="Text_011b9813f17f41a5b27a5e52aa0fa32d9">
<div><br/>
    </div>
</ix:continuation></ix:continuation>
    <ix:continuation id="Text_3352c7f9313745d9830a22d42ede9cba6" continuedAt="Text_3352c7f9313745d9830a22d42ede9cba7"><ix:continuation id="Text_011b9813f17f41a5b27a5e52aa0fa32d9" continuedAt="Text_011b9813f17f41a5b27a5e52aa0fa32d10">
<div style="text-align: justify; font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">In addition, the Company provides certain health care benefits for retired employees. Benefits were accrued over the employees&#8217; active service period. Only employees
      that were employed by the Company on or before January 1, 2000 are eligible to receive post-retirement health care benefits.&#160;The Plan is contributory for participating retirees, requiring participants to absorb certain deductibles and coinsurance
      amounts with contributions adjusted annually to reflect cost sharing provisions and benefit limitations called for in the Plan. Employees become eligible for these benefits if they reach normal retirement age while working for the Company.&#160;For
      eligible employees described above, the Company funds the cost of post-retirement health care as benefits are paid. The Company elected to recognize the transition obligation on a delayed basis over <ix:nonNumeric name="nbtb:TransitionObligationPeriodOfRecognition" id="Fact_0b260a9ee71d472e9eb3c324514c5c7a" contextRef="c20250101to20251231" format="ixt-sec:durwordsen">twenty years</ix:nonNumeric>. These post-retirement benefits are referred to herein as &#8220;Other Benefits.&#8221;</div>
</ix:continuation></ix:continuation>
    <ix:continuation id="Text_3352c7f9313745d9830a22d42ede9cba7" continuedAt="Text_3352c7f9313745d9830a22d42ede9cba8"><ix:continuation id="Text_011b9813f17f41a5b27a5e52aa0fa32d10" continuedAt="Text_011b9813f17f41a5b27a5e52aa0fa32d11">
<div><br/>
    </div>
</ix:continuation></ix:continuation>
    <ix:continuation id="Text_3352c7f9313745d9830a22d42ede9cba8" continuedAt="Text_3352c7f9313745d9830a22d42ede9cba9"><ix:continuation id="Text_011b9813f17f41a5b27a5e52aa0fa32d11" continuedAt="Text_011b9813f17f41a5b27a5e52aa0fa32d12">
<div style="text-align: justify; color: rgb(0, 0, 0); font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">Accounting standards require an employer to: (1) recognize the overfunded or underfunded status of defined benefit post-retirement plans, which is
      measured as the difference between plan assets at fair value and the benefit obligation, as an asset or liability in its balance sheet; (2) recognize changes in that funded status in the year in which the changes occur through comprehensive income;
      and (3) measure the defined benefit plan assets and obligations as of the date of its year-end balance sheet.</div>
</ix:continuation></ix:continuation>

<div style="text-align: justify; font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">For measurement purposes, the annual rates of increase in the per capita cost of covered medical and prescription drug benefits for fiscal year 2025 were assumed to be <ix:nonFraction name="us-gaap:DefinedBenefitPlanHealthCareCostTrendRateAssumedNextFiscalYear" id="Fact_411aa3db7e3146b3827c7c33fe2fa64b" contextRef="c20251231_RangeAxis_MinimumMember" unitRef="U005" decimals="3" scale="-2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal">6.5</ix:nonFraction>% to <ix:nonFraction name="us-gaap:DefinedBenefitPlanHealthCareCostTrendRateAssumedNextFiscalYear" id="Fact_bd2efef021d44339bc0d1724d6b5c56a" contextRef="c20251231_RangeAxis_MaximumMember" unitRef="U005" decimals="4" scale="-2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal">11.25</ix:nonFraction>%. The rates were assumed to
      decrease gradually to <ix:nonFraction name="us-gaap:DefinedBenefitPlanUltimateHealthCareCostTrendRate1" id="Fact_9d7d05f6558a4fc393287b3df7c90755" contextRef="c20251231" unitRef="U005" decimals="3" scale="-2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal">4.5</ix:nonFraction>% for fiscal year 2034 and remain at that level thereafter.&#160;Assumed health care cost trend rates have a
      significant effect on amounts reported for health care plans.</div>
</ix:continuation>
    <div>
      <ix:continuation id="Text_011b9813f17f41a5b27a5e52aa0fa32d42" continuedAt="Text_011b9813f17f41a5b27a5e52aa0fa32d43"><ix:continuation id="Text_3352c7f9313745d9830a22d42ede9cba9" continuedAt="Text_3352c7f9313745d9830a22d42ede9cba10">
<div><br/>
      </div>
</ix:continuation></ix:continuation>
    </div>

    <ix:continuation id="Text_011b9813f17f41a5b27a5e52aa0fa32d43" continuedAt="Text_011b9813f17f41a5b27a5e52aa0fa32d44"><ix:continuation id="Text_3352c7f9313745d9830a22d42ede9cba10" continuedAt="Text_3352c7f9313745d9830a22d42ede9cba11">
<div style="text-align: justify; font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; font-weight: bold;">Plan Investment Policy</div>
</ix:continuation></ix:continuation>
    <ix:continuation id="Text_011b9813f17f41a5b27a5e52aa0fa32d44" continuedAt="Text_011b9813f17f41a5b27a5e52aa0fa32d45"><ix:continuation id="Text_3352c7f9313745d9830a22d42ede9cba11" continuedAt="Text_3352c7f9313745d9830a22d42ede9cba12">
<div><br/>
    </div>
</ix:continuation></ix:continuation>
    <ix:continuation id="Text_011b9813f17f41a5b27a5e52aa0fa32d45" continuedAt="Text_011b9813f17f41a5b27a5e52aa0fa32d46"><ix:continuation id="Text_3352c7f9313745d9830a22d42ede9cba12" continuedAt="Text_3352c7f9313745d9830a22d42ede9cba13">
<div style="text-align: justify; font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">The Company&#8217;s key investment objectives in managing its defined benefit plan assets are to ensure that present and future benefit obligations to all participants and
      beneficiaries are met as they become due; to provide a total return that, over the long-term, maximizes the ratio of the plan assets to liabilities, while minimizing the present value of required Company contributions, at the appropriate levels of
      risk; to meet statutory requirements and regulatory agencies&#8217; requirements; and to satisfy applicable accounting standards.&#160;The Company periodically evaluates the asset allocations, funded status, rate of return assumption and contribution strategy
      for satisfaction of our investment objectives.&#160;</div>
</ix:continuation></ix:continuation>

      Stock Plan, equity-based awards are granted to directors and employees to increase their direct proprietary interest in the operations and success of the Company.&#160;The Stock Plan assumed all prior equity-based incentive plans and any new equity-based
      awards are granted under the terms of the Stock Plan.&#160;<span style="font-size: 10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman'; color: rgb(0, 0, 0);">Restricted shares granted under the Plan typically vest after </span><span style="-sec-ix-hidden:Fact_0586e264087149579150a9f2ad9bc9d5">three</span><span style="font-size: 10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman'; color: rgb(0, 0, 0);"> or </span><ix:nonNumeric name="us-gaap:ShareBasedCompensationArrangementByShareBasedPaymentAwardAwardVestingPeriod1" id="Fact_b9028afdb7974d89904f436df98c1fc7" contextRef="c20250101to20251231_AwardTypeAxis_RestrictedStockMember_RangeAxis_MaximumMember_TitleOfIndividualAxis_EmployeesMember" format="ixt-sec:durwordsen">five years</ix:nonNumeric> for employees and <ix:nonNumeric name="us-gaap:ShareBasedCompensationArrangementByShareBasedPaymentAwardAwardVestingPeriod1" id="Fact_c11d11b9e81d4b5e912c8435a2435279" contextRef="c20250101to20251231_AwardTypeAxis_RestrictedStockMember_RangeAxis_MinimumMember_TitleOfIndividualAxis_DirectorMember" format="ixt-sec:durwordsen">one year</ix:nonNumeric> for non-employee directors. Restricted
      stock units granted under the Stock Plan may have different terms and conditions.&#160;Performance shares and units granted under the Stock Plan for executives may have different terms and conditions. Since 2011, the Company primarily grants restricted
      stock unit awards.           terms of the Stock Plan, stock options are granted to purchase shares of the Company&#8217;s common stock at a price equal to the fair market value of the common stock on the date of the grant. Shares issued as a result of vesting of restricted stock
          unit awards and stock option exercises are funded from the Company&#8217;s treasury stoc</span>k.</span></div>

<div style="text-align: justify; font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">Certain restrictions exist regarding the ability of the Bank to transfer funds to the Company in the form of cash dividends. The approval of the OCC is required to pay
      dividends when a bank fails to meet certain minimum regulatory capital standards or when such dividends are in excess of a subsidiary bank&#8217;s earnings retained in the current year plus retained net profits for the preceding <ix:nonNumeric name="nbtb:PrecedingPeriodOfRetainedNetProfitsForApprovalOfOfficeOfComptrollerOfCurrency" id="Fact_cff4fcffd32a4cc7bb5f669e362a927d" contextRef="c20250101to20251231" format="ixt-sec:durwordsen">two years</ix:nonNumeric> as specified in applicable OCC regulations.&#160;At December 31, 2025, approximately $<ix:nonFraction name="us-gaap:StatutoryAccountingPracticesStatutoryAmountAvailableForDividendPayments" id="Fact_c8f333f0f6c141c2a258ff98b8013f1d" contextRef="c20251231" unitRef="U001" decimals="-5" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal">115.9</ix:nonFraction> million of the total stockholders&#8217; equity of the Bank
      was available for payment of dividends to the Company without approval by the OCC. The Bank&#8217;s ability to pay dividends also is subject to the Bank being in compliance with regulatory capital requirements.&#160;The Bank is currently in compliance with
      these requirements. Under the State of Delaware General Corporation Law, the Company may declare and pay dividends either out of accumulated net retained earnings or capital surplus.</div>
</ix:continuation>

Pursuant to the amended stock repurchase program, the Company may repurchase up to <ix:nonFraction name="srt:StockRepurchaseProgramNumberOfSharesAuthorizedToBeRepurchased" id="Fact_849b3d48fe0b4339a5fd8f7409a0c036" contextRef="c20251027" unitRef="U002" decimals="0" scale="0" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal">2,000,000</ix:nonFraction> shares of the Company&#8217;s common stock with all repurchases under the stock repurchase program to be made by December 31, 2027. <div style="text-align: justify; font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;"><span style="font-size: 10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-weight: bold;">15.</span>&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;<span style="font-size: 10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-weight: bold;">Regulatory Capital Requirements</span></div>
</ix:nonNumeric>
    <div style="text-align: justify; font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">
      <ix:continuation id="Text_a3f73d7de4084ba49d4dc6e85c9d49bc1" continuedAt="Text_a3f73d7de4084ba49d4dc6e85c9d49bc2"><hr style="height: 2px; color: #000000; background-color: #000000; text-align: center; border: none; margin-left: auto; margin-right: auto;"/></ix:continuation></div>

    <ix:continuation id="Text_a3f73d7de4084ba49d4dc6e85c9d49bc2" continuedAt="Text_a3f73d7de4084ba49d4dc6e85c9d49bc3">
<div><br/>
    </div>
</ix:continuation>
    <ix:continuation id="Text_a3f73d7de4084ba49d4dc6e85c9d49bc3" continuedAt="Text_a3f73d7de4084ba49d4dc6e85c9d49bc4">
<div style="text-align: justify; font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">The Company and the Bank are subject to various regulatory capital requirements administered by the federal banking agencies.&#160;Failure to meet minimum capital
      requirements can initiate certain mandatory and possibly additional discretionary actions by regulators that, if undertaken, could have a direct material effect on the consolidated financial statements. Under capital adequacy guidelines and the
      regulatory framework for prompt corrective action, the Bank must meet specific capital guidelines that involve quantitative measures of NBT Bank&#8217;s assets, liabilities and certain off-balance sheet items as calculated under regulatory accounting
      practices. The capital amounts and classifications are also subject to qualitative judgments by the regulators about components, risk weightings and other factors.</div>
</ix:continuation>
    <ix:continuation id="Text_a3f73d7de4084ba49d4dc6e85c9d49bc4" continuedAt="Text_a3f73d7de4084ba49d4dc6e85c9d49bc5">
<div><br/>
    </div>
</ix:continuation>
    <ix:continuation id="Text_a3f73d7de4084ba49d4dc6e85c9d49bc5" continuedAt="Text_a3f73d7de4084ba49d4dc6e85c9d49bc6">
<div style="text-align: justify; font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">Quantitative measures established by regulation to ensure capital adequacy require the Company and the Bank to maintain minimum amounts and ratios (set forth in the
      table below) of total and Tier 1 Capital to risk-weighted assets and of Tier 1 capital to average assets. <span style="font-size: 10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman'; color: rgb(0, 0, 0);">In addition to maintaining minimum capital ratios, the
        Company is subject to a capital conservation buffer (&#8220;Buffer&#8221;) of 2.50% above the minimum to avoid restriction on capital distributions and discretionary bonus paychecks to officers. At&#160;</span>December 31, 2025<span style="font-size: 10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman'; color: rgb(0, 0, 0);">&#160;and&#160;</span>2024, the Company and the Bank meet all capital adequacy requirements to which they were subject.</div>
</ix:continuation>
    <ix:continuation id="Text_a3f73d7de4084ba49d4dc6e85c9d49bc6" continuedAt="Text_a3f73d7de4084ba49d4dc6e85c9d49bc7">
<div><br/>
    </div>
</ix:continuation>
    <ix:continuation id="Text_a3f73d7de4084ba49d4dc6e85c9d49bc7" continuedAt="Text_a3f73d7de4084ba49d4dc6e85c9d49bc8">
<div style="text-align: justify; font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">Under their prompt corrective action regulations, regulatory authorities are required to take certain supervisory actions (and may take additional discretionary actions)
      with respect to an undercapitalized institution. Such actions could have a direct material effect on an institution&#8217;s financial statements.&#160;The regulations establish a framework for the classification of banks into five categories:&#160;well-capitalized,
      adequately capitalized, undercapitalized, significantly undercapitalized and critically undercapitalized. As of December 31, 2025 and 2024, the most recent notifications from the Bank&#8217;s regulators categorized the Bank as well-capitalized under the regulatory framework for prompt
      corrective action.&#160;To be categorized as well-capitalized the Bank must maintain minimum total risk-based, Tier 1 risk-based and Tier 1 Capital to Average Asset ratios as set forth in the table below. There are no conditions or events since that
      notification that management believes have changed the Bank&#8217;s category.</div>
</ix:continuation>

<div style="text-align: justify; font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;"><span style="font-size: 10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-weight: bold;">18.</span>&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;<span style="font-size: 10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-weight: bold;">Commitments and Contingent Liabilities</span></div>

      lines of credit, commitments to originate new loans and loans sold with recourse generally follow the loan classifications.</div>

<div style="text-align: justify; font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">At December 31, 2025, approximately <ix:nonFraction name="nbtb:PercentageOfCompanysLoansSecuredByRealEstate" id="Fact_e9264295cf09499f8b0e3284de8b8389" contextRef="c20251231" unitRef="U005" decimals="2" scale="-2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal">67</ix:nonFraction>% of the Company&#8217;s
      loans were secured by real estate located in upstate New York, northeastern Pennsylvania, southern New Hampshire, western Massachusetts, Vermont, southern Maine and central and northwestern Connecticut. Accordingly, the ultimate collectability of a
      substantial portion of the Company&#8217;s portfolio is susceptible to changes in market conditions of those areas. Management is not aware of any material concentrations of credit to any industry or individual borrowers.</div>
